note: Claim registry. Only claims with approvedForPublication=true may enter production copy. Every claim names the source section carrying the quoted operative language, never a homepage or a definitions section.

claims.claim: Idaho law permits only one countywide highway district to operate within a county that has voted to form one.
claims.quotedLanguage: Only one (1) county-wide highway district shall be operative within a county where the electorate has voted affirmatively for the formation of a county-wide highway district.

claims.claim: A city inside a countywide highway district may not maintain or supervise city highways, and may not levy ad valorem taxes for their construction, repair or maintenance.
claims.quotedLanguage: No city included within a county-wide highway district shall maintain or supervise any city highways or levy any ad valorem taxes for the construction, repair or maintenance of city highways.
claims.notes: This is the statutory basis for the ACHD arrangement. It has no California analogue and is the single strongest jurisdiction differentiator found. NOTE: the statute is general Idaho law; a separate source is required to establish that ACHD is in fact Ada County's countywide district — see claim achd-is-ada-district, which is NOT yet verified.

claims.claim: A single countywide highway district is responsible for design, construction, reconstruction and maintenance of city rights-of-way and their curbs, gutters, culverts, sidewalks, paved medians, bulkheads and retaining walls.
claims.quotedLanguage: shall be responsible for the design, construction, reconstruction and maintenance of city rights-of-way and accompanying curbs, gutters, culverts, sidewalks, paved medians, bulkheads and retaining walls
claims.notes: Directly seller-relevant: sidewalk and approach questions on an Ada County property are a district matter, not a city one.

claims.claim: Cities within a countywide highway district retain responsibility for pre-existing local improvement district bonds, may spend city funds on trees, shrubs, grass and other plants in rights-of-way, and control parking meters.
claims.quotedLanguage: jurisdiction and responsibility for outstanding local improvement district bonds or warrants sold or issued by the city prior to dissolution of the city highway system

claims.claim: Ada County Development Services controls no roadway infrastructure within the county's boundaries; the Ada County Highway District leads identification and development of transportation projects and maintains the county's Master Street Map.
claims.quotedLanguage: While Ada County Development Services does not control any roadway infrastructure within its boundaries, these plans help us to be better partners with partner agencies and our residents.
claims.notes: NARROWED from the original claim. This Tier 1 county source establishes that the county itself controls no roads and that ACHD leads transportation — it does NOT independently state that ACHD maintains roads inside each incorporated city. That specific proposition still rests on the general statutes (40-1406, 40-1415) plus the premise that Ada County has a countywide district. achdidaho.org returns 403 to automated fetches. Do not write 'ACHD maintains every road inside Boise' until a direct ACHD or ITD source is captured.

claims.claim: Idaho's homestead exemption protecting home equity from creditors is capped at $175,000, regardless of the area of land.
claims.quotedLanguage: A homestead may consist of lands, as described in section 55-1001, Idaho Code, regardless of area, but the homestead exemption amount shall not exceed the sum of one hundred seventy-five thousand dollars ($175,000).
claims.notes: ⚠️ DO NOT CONFUSE with the property-tax homeowner's exemption (Idaho Code 63-602G, $125,000). These are different statutes doing different jobs and Ada County's own website calls BOTH 'Homestead Exemption'. See claim id-homeowners-tax-exemption-125k.

claims.claim: Idaho's homestead property-tax exemption removes from taxation the lesser of the first $125,000 of the homestead's market value for assessment purposes, or 50% of that market value.
claims.quotedLanguage: For each tax year, the first one hundred twenty-five thousand dollars ($125,000) of the market value for assessment purposes of the homestead as that term is defined in section 63-701, Idaho Code, or fifty percent (50%) of the market value for assessment purposes of the homestead as that term is defined in section 63-701, Idaho Code, whichever is the lesser, shall be exempt from property taxation.
claims.notes: ⚠️ TERMINOLOGY TRAP: this is NOT Idaho Code 55-1003 (creditor-protection homestead, $125,000 vs $175,000 caps, different purposes). Ada County's own site calls both 'Homestead Exemption'. Any page using that phrase must say which is meant. FUTURE-DATING CHECKED: the statute page states 'Idaho Statutes are updated to the website July 1 following the legislative session'; the most recent amendment is 2026 ch. 236 and, today being after 1 July 2026, the displayed text is in force. The $125,000 figure is independently corroborated by the Ada County Assessor. The acreage limit is NOT in this section — see id-homestead-one-acre-limit. 🚨 RED-TEAM FINDING 1: the effective date of the 2026 amendment (ch. 236) is UNCONFIRMED. The statute page carries no effective-date line, and a secondary result suggests 1 January 2026, which does not reconcile with the site's July-1 posting convention. The $125,000 figure is independently corroborated by the Ada County Assessor, so the figure itself is unlikely to be wrong, but the 2026 session law must be read before any page states this exemption. ⚠️ amendmentHistory REPAIRED 2026-09-10. The stored string was ELIDED — it read 'added 1996, ch. 98, sec. 7 ... am. 2024' with a literal ellipsis standing in for roughly twenty amendments. Rendering that under the verbatim rule would have presented an abridged quote as a whole one, which is the precise failure the quote regime exists to prevent. Replaced with the compiler's complete history note from the cached statute page. The elision was invisible for as long as it existed because nothing verified amendmentHistory at all; verify-quotes now checks it against the cache like any other verbatim string. SUPERSEDED 2026-11-12 by pt-homestead-exemption-cap-in-force-2026, which verifies the 2026 amendment (ch. 236, H0843) took effect retroactively to 2026-01-01. Keep this one held; cite the new id.

claims.claim: To qualify for the homeowner's exemption for a tax year, an owner must own and occupy the home on or before the last county business day in December and file the application by close of business that same day; once approved it need only be re-filed on a move or a change of ownership.
claims.quotedLanguage: To qualify, you must own and occupy your home on or before the last county business day in December. You must also submit an application to our office by the close of business on that same day for the current tax year. Once approved, you only need to reapply if you move or if ownership of the property changes.
claims.notes: Directly relevant to sellers: a change of ownership ends the exemption's automatic carry-forward, so a buyer must re-apply.

claims.claim: Idaho law requires all non-exempt property to be assessed at market value as of January 1, and January 1 is also the lien date for real property.
claims.quotedLanguage: Idaho law requires that all non-exempt property be assessed at market value as of January 1st.
claims.notes: The lien-date statement is a separate sentence on the same page: 'The lien date for real property and most personal property is January 1.'

claims.claim: All Ada County property is assessed every year, but state law requires a physical inspection every five years; roughly 20% of county properties are reappraised in a given year and the rest are trended on market conditions.
claims.quotedLanguage: State law requires properties to be physically inspected every 5 years. Roughly 20% of the properties within the county are reappraised in any given year. During the other four years of the cycle, values are trended based on market conditions.
claims.notes: Explains to a seller why an assessed value can diverge from a current market view — genuinely useful, and a natural bridge to the offer-math page.

claims.claim: The Ada County Assessor estimates what a typical buyer would reasonably pay for a property as of January 1 rather than setting its value.
claims.quotedLanguage: Remember: The assessor does not set a value for your property. He or she just estimates what a typical buyer would reasonably pay for it on January 1st.

claims.claim: Whether an item is real property or personal property in Idaho is decided by a three-factor test of annexation, adaptation and intent; an item satisfying all three is a fixture and therefore real property.
claims.quotedLanguage: If an item of property satisfies all three factors of the three factor test, the item becomes a fixture and therefore real property
claims.notes: Load-bearing for the manufactured-home pillar: whether a manufactured home is real or personal property changes how it is sold and conveyed.

claims.claim: Ada County's residential appraisers value detached single-family dwellings, attached townhomes, condominium units, multi-family residential up to four units, and manufactured housing; apartments and higher-density residential are handled by commercial appraisers.
claims.quotedLanguage: Ada County's residential appraisers manage the valuation of all residential property types, including detached single-family dwellings, attached townhomes, condominium units, multi-family residential up to four-units, and manufactured housing.
claims.notes: The four-unit line is a useful boundary for the small-multifamily property-type page.

claims.claim: An Idaho trust deed foreclosure requires notice of the trustee's sale to be given at least 120 days before the day fixed for the sale.
claims.quotedLanguage: at least one hundred twenty (120) days before the day fixed by the trustee for the trustee's sale, notice of such sale shall be given
claims.notes: The single most useful number for a distressed Idaho seller. Do NOT describe this as 'the foreclosure timeline' — it is one statutory minimum within a longer process.

claims.claim: Notice of an Idaho trustee's sale must be published in a newspaper of general circulation in each county where the property sits, once a week for four successive weeks, with the last publication at least 30 days before the sale.
claims.quotedLanguage: published in a newspaper of general circulation in each of the counties in which the property is situated once a week for four (4) successive weeks...with the last publication to be at least thirty (30) days prior to the day of sale
claims.notes: 'each of the counties in which the property is situated' matters for Star, which spans Ada and Canyon.

claims.claim: At least three good-faith attempts at personal service must be made on different days over a period of not less than seven days, each at least 30 days before an Idaho trustee's sale.
claims.quotedLanguage: At least three (3) good faith attempts shall be made on different days over a period of not less than seven (7) days, each of which attempts must be made at least thirty (30) days prior to the day of the sale

claims.claim: Star is an incorporated city lying in both Ada County and Canyon County.
claims.quotedLanguage: ID|16|76870|Star city|Incorporated Place|A|Ada County, Canyon County
claims.notes: Never describe Star as wholly within Ada County. Any jurisdiction-dependent statement about Star must say which county part is meant.

claims.claim: Ada County's estimated resident population was 535,799 in 2024.
claims.notes: ⚠️ An estimate, not a count — always label it as Census Population Estimates, Vintage 2024. A commonly-repeated figure of ~557,590 for Ada County 2024 conflicts with this; see claim ada-population-disputed-557590.

claims.claim: Two authoritative estimates of Ada County's 2024 population coexist and differ by about 4%: COMPASS puts it at 557,590; the U.S. Census Bureau's Population Estimates, Vintage 2024, puts it at 535,799.
claims.quotedLanguage: According to COMPASS estimates, Ada County's population reached 557,590 in 2024, with the majority (88.6%) living in one of the County's six cities.
claims.notes: RESOLVED — the 557,590 figure is COMPASS (the regional planning association), published by Ada County; 535,799 is Census PEP Vintage 2024. Neither is wrong. ⚠️ EVERY published population figure must name its source. Never mix the two families in one comparison, and never compute growth across them.

claims.claim: Population growth across Ada County's cities diverged sharply between the 2020 census base and the 2024 estimate: Star +61.4%, Kuna +21.0%, Meridian +18.6%, Eagle +7.4%, Garden City +5.1%, Boise +1.0%.
claims.notes: Computed WITHIN one vintage (2020 base and 2024 estimate from the same Vintage 2024 file). Never compute growth across vintages. This is the strongest city-differentiation fact found so far: Boise is effectively static while Star has grown by nearly two thirds.

claims.claim: For Idaho property-tax purposes a homestead is the owner-occupied primary dwelling plus no more than one acre of surrounding land reasonably necessary for its use as a home.
claims.quotedLanguage: "Homestead" means the dwelling, owner-occupied by the claimant as described in this chapter and used as the primary dwelling place of the claimant and may be occupied by any members of the household as their home, and so much of the land surrounding it, not exceeding one (1) acre, as is reasonably necessary for the use of the dwelling as a home.
claims.notes: Directly relevant to acreage sellers: land beyond one acre gets no homestead exemption, so a 5-acre parcel is taxed very differently from a 0.9-acre lot. Cited to 63-701 because 63-602G defines the dollar cap but delegates the definition of 'homestead' — citing 63-602G for the acreage would send a reader to a section that does not contain it.

claims.claim: Idaho requires a seller of residential real property of one to four dwelling units — including non-owner-occupied rental property — to complete a property condition disclosure form, unless the transfer is exempt.
claims.quotedLanguage: Any person who intends to transfer any residential real property, including nonowner occupied rental property, on or after July 1, 1994, by any of the methods as set forth herein shall complete all applicable items in a property disclosure form prescribed under section 55-2508, Idaho Code. Except as provided in section 55-2505, Idaho Code, this chapter applies to any transfer by sale, exchange, installment sale contract, a lease with an option to purchase, any other option to purchase, or ground lease coupled with improvements, of real property improved with or consisting of not less than one (1) nor more than four (4) dwelling units.
claims.notes: ⚠️ CONTENT HONESTY: many cash-buyer sites imply an as-is sale means no disclosure. In Idaho the duty applies to 1-4 unit residential by default and is removed only by a listed exemption (55-2505). Never write 'no disclosures needed' as a general statement.

claims.claim: Idaho's property condition disclosure requirement does not apply to a transfer ordered by a probate court during administration of a decedent's estate, nor to a transfer by a fiduciary in the course of administering a decedent's estate, guardianship, conservatorship or trust.
claims.quotedLanguage: (1) A transfer pursuant to court order including, but not limited to, a transfer ordered by a probate court during the administration of a decedent's estate ... (7) A transfer by a fiduciary in the course of the administration of a decedent's estate, a guardianship, a conservatorship, or a trust;
claims.notes: Directly answers the most common inherited-property question. Note the two exemptions are distinct: (1) turns on a court order, (7) on the seller's fiduciary capacity. Do not merge them — a personal representative selling without a court order relies on (7), not (1).

claims.claim: Idaho's property condition disclosure requirement does not apply to a transfer between spouses or former spouses resulting from a decree of divorce, dissolution, annulment or legal separation, or from a property settlement agreement incidental to one.
claims.quotedLanguage: (10) A transfer between spouses or former spouses as a result of a decree of divorce, dissolution of marriage, annulment, or legal separation or as a result of a property settlement agreement incidental to a decree of divorce, dissolution of marriage, annulment, or legal separation;
claims.notes: ⚠️ NARROW. The exemption covers a transfer BETWEEN THE SPOUSES. A divorcing couple selling to a third party is not exempt on this ground. Getting this wrong would tell a divorcing seller they owe no disclosure when they do.

claims.claim: Idaho's property condition disclosure requirement does not apply to a deed in lieu of foreclosure, a transfer to a deed-of-trust beneficiary by a trustor in default, a foreclosure sale, or a sale under a power of sale following default occurring within one year of foreclosure on the default.
claims.quotedLanguage: (2) A transfer to a mortgagee by a mortgagor by deed in lieu of foreclosure or in satisfaction of the mortgage debt; (3) A transfer to a beneficiary of a deed of trust by a trustor in default; (4) A transfer by a foreclosure sale that follows a default in the satisfaction of an obligation secured by a mortgage; (5) A transfer by a sale under a power of sale following a default in the satisfaction of an obligation that is secured by a deed of trust or another instrument containing a power of sale occurring within one (1) year of foreclosure on the default;
claims.notes: ⚠️ These exemptions describe transfers INTO or OUT OF the foreclosure process, not an ordinary pre-foreclosure sale by an owner still holding title. An owner behind on payments who sells to a cash buyer before any trustee's sale is NOT exempt on these grounds. This is the single easiest disclosure error to make on a foreclosure page.

claims.claim: An Idaho buyer who receives the property condition disclosure form after entering a transfer agreement may rescind within three business days of receiving it, based on a specific objection identified in the notice, and is entitled to the return of deposits; the right is waived if no signed notice is delivered in that window.
claims.quotedLanguage: a rescission of a transfer agreement may only occur if the transferee's written, signed and dated document of rescission is delivered to the transferor or his agent or subagent within three (3) business days following the date on which the transferee or his agent receives the property disclosure form prescribed under section 55-2508, Idaho Code. If no signed notice of rescission is received by the transferor within the three (3) day period, transferee's right to rescind is waived.
claims.notes: Rescission must rest on a specific objection to a disclosure, not on a change of mind. Useful for explaining certainty of close honestly.

claims.claim: Until the appointment terminates, an Idaho personal representative has the same power over the title to estate property that an absolute owner would have — held in trust for creditors and others interested in the estate — and that power may be exercised without notice, hearing or court order.
claims.quotedLanguage: Until termination of his appointment a personal representative has the same power over the title to property of the estate that an absolute owner would have, in trust however, for the benefit of the creditors and others interested in the estate. This power may be exercised without notice, hearing, or order of court.
claims.notes: ⚠️ MUST BE STATED WITH id-pr-powers-limited-by-will. 15-3-715 opens 'Except as restricted or otherwise provided by the will or by an order in a formal proceeding', so the 'without court order' power is a default, not an absolute. Publishing 15-3-711 alone would tell an heir they can always sell without court involvement. Also note the power belongs to an APPOINTED personal representative — it says nothing about an heir who has not been appointed.

claims.claim: An Idaho personal representative's authorised transactions are subject to any restriction in the will or an order in a formal proceeding, and to the statutory priorities for claims against the estate.
claims.quotedLanguage: Except as restricted or otherwise provided by the will or by an order in a formal proceeding and subject to the priorities stated in section 15-3-902 of this code, a personal representative, acting reasonably for the benefit of the interested persons, may properly:
claims.notes: The necessary qualifier on id-pr-power-over-title. Never publish one without the other.

claims.claim: Idaho defines domestic water use as use for homes, camps, campgrounds and livestock including irrigation of up to half an acre, provided total use does not exceed 13,000 gallons per day; or any other use not exceeding 2.8 acre-feet per year.
claims.quotedLanguage: The use of water for homes, organization camps, public campgrounds, livestock, and for any other purpose in connection therewith, including irrigation of up to one-half (1/2) acre of land, if the total use does not exceed thirteen thousand (13,000) gallons per day; or 2. The use of water for any other purpose, if the total use does not exceed a diversion volume of two and eight-tenths (2.8) acre feet per year.
claims.notes: ⚠️ FAST-MOVING LAW. Amended 2025 ch. 129 AND 2026 ch. 2 — twice in two years. Re-verify before every publication or refresh of any water/well page. The half-acre irrigation figure is the number that most affects a rural Ada County buyer's expectations about watering a larger lot.

claims.claim: Idaho's domestic water definition excludes mobile home and RV parks, apartments, condominiums and similar multiple-dwelling developments, subdivisions, and commercial or business establishments, unless the use stays within the 2.8 acre-foot annual limit.
claims.quotedLanguage: "Domestic purposes" or "domestic uses" shall not include water for the following purposes, unless the use meets the diversion volume limitations set forth in paragraph (a)(i)2. of this subsection: 1. Mobile home parks or recreational vehicle parks; 2. Apartments, condominiums, and similar developments with multiple dwelling units; 3. Subdivisions, except as provided in subsection (3) of this section; or 4. Commercial or business establishments or mixed-use establishments where the water is used primarily for commercial or business purposes.
claims.notes: Load-bearing for development-land and small-multifamily pages: a domestic well does not carry a subdivision or a multi-unit development. This is a real constraint on what a rural Ada County parcel can become.

claims.claim: For Idaho's domestic water statutes a subdivision is a tract divided into five or more lots, parcels or sites for sale or building development, excluding a bona fide division of agricultural land into lots of five acres or larger maintained as agricultural land.
claims.quotedLanguage: "Subdivision" means a tract of land divided into five (5) or more lots, parcels, or sites for the purpose of sale or building development, whether immediate or future; provided that this definition shall not include a bona fide division or partition of agricultural land for agricultural purposes.
claims.notes: ⚠️ This five-lot threshold is the WATER-STATUTE definition. It is not necessarily the planning or platting definition used by Ada County Development Services or by a city. Never state a single 'Idaho subdivision threshold' across both domains without verifying the land-use definition separately.

claims.claim: Central District Health's Environmental Health Division permits septic systems, reviews land development applications and verifies the location of shallow injection wells across Ada, Boise, Elmore and Valley counties.
claims.quotedLanguage: Environmental Health Specialists at Central District Health (CDH) permit septic systems, review land development applications and verify location of shallow injection wells to ensure reliable and safe water resources for the community.
claims.notes: JURISDICTION DIFFERENTIATOR: septic in Ada County is a PUBLIC HEALTH DISTRICT matter, not a city or county building-department matter. A seller with a septic question is directed to CDH, not to Boise or Ada County permitting. CDH's remit spans four counties, so it is not an Ada-only body.

claims.claim: Ada County's planning division processes land use applications only in unincorporated Ada County; land use inside an incorporated city is that city's jurisdiction.
claims.quotedLanguage: Our planning division processes land use applications in unincorporated Ada County and works with the Ada County Historic Preservation Council...
claims.notes: ⚠️ THE MOST IMPORTANT JURISDICTION FACT FOR CONTENT. 64,427 people live in unincorporated Ada County. Their zoning, platting and permitting authority is the COUNTY. Everyone inside Boise, Meridian, Eagle, Kuna, Star or Garden City deals with their CITY. Any page that says 'contact Ada County for permits' is wrong for 88% of county residents.

claims.claim: Ada County's engineering and surveying division reviews preliminary plats, drainage plans, private roads, hillside applications, floodplain permits and property boundary adjustments in unincorporated Ada County.
claims.quotedLanguage: Our engineering and surveying division reviews preliminary plats, drainage plans, private roads, hillside applications, floodplain permits, and property boundary adjustments in unincorporated Ada County.
claims.notes: Directly maps to the difficult-property and land pillars: private roads, hillside applications, floodplain permits and boundary adjustments are exactly the problems a land seller has. Note the scope is unincorporated ONLY.

claims.claim: Ada County's building division reviews plans and inspects buildings, and its permitting division accepts building, manufactured home and mechanical permit applications through a client portal.
claims.quotedLanguage: Our building division reviews plans and inspects buildings to ensure Ada County residents are safe in any building they walk into.
claims.notes: The page does not state whether building inspection extends inside cities; do not assert that it does. Manufactured home permits are explicitly named, which matters for the manufactured-housing pillar.

claims.claim: The Ada County Treasurer serves as ex officio tax collector, responsible for collecting the property taxes levied by all taxing districts including cities and schools.
claims.quotedLanguage: The Treasurer serves as ex officio tax collector, responsible for the collection of property taxes levied by the taxing districts, including cities and schools.
claims.notes: Completes the tax split: the ASSESSOR values, the TREASURER collects, and the collection is county-wide across every city and school district. A seller with a delinquency question goes to the Treasurer, not the Assessor.

claims.claim: The Ada County Treasurer also serves as ex officio public administrator, responsible for administering the estates of decedents who have no one to administer the estate.
claims.quotedLanguage: The Treasurer also serves as ex officio public administrator, responsible for administering the estates of decedents without a person to administer the estate.
claims.notes: Obscure and genuinely useful: an Ada County property whose owner died with no one to administer the estate falls to the TREASURER as public administrator. No competitor cash-buyer site will carry this.

claims.claim: The Ada County Recorder's Office maintains all documents related to property ownership within the county, and under Idaho Code 31-2419 all recorded documents are open to public inspection and available for purchase online.
claims.quotedLanguage: The Ada County Recorder's Office maintains all documents related to property ownership within the County. ... Pursuant to Idaho Code § 31-2419, all recorded documents are open for public inspection and available for purchase online.
claims.notes: Recording is county-wide regardless of which city a property sits in. The statutory cite for public inspection is 31-2419 (taken from the county page; not yet read at the Legislature).

claims.claim: When recording a document in Ada County, redacting personal identifying information is the responsibility of the party submitting it, not the Recorder's office.
claims.quotedLanguage: If you are submitting documents for recording, it is the responsibility of the party submitting to redact any personal identifying information (PII), such as social security number, date of birth and any account numbers. This is not the responsibility of the Recorder's office to identify and redact personal identifying information (PII).
claims.notes: Practical and seller-relevant, and a genuine trap: recorded documents are public and nobody upstream will redact for you.

claims.claim: The Ada County Court Assistance Office's eviction forms may be used only to evict a tenant who has not paid rent; they cannot be used to evict a tenant current on rent, to sue for back rent, or to move a mobile home from a rented space.
claims.quotedLanguage: Eviction forms on our site can only be used to evict a tenant who has not paid rent. You cannot use our forms to evict a tenant who is up to date on their rent, sue for back rent or move a mobile home from a rented space.
claims.notes: ⚠️ Use carefully. This describes the SELF-HELP FORMS' scope, not the limits of Idaho eviction law. Never write 'you can only evict for non-payment in Idaho' — that would be false. The page itself says its assistance is no substitute for legal advice, and our pages must not read as legal advice either.

claims.claim: Each incorporated city in Ada County administers land use and zoning within its own city limits through its own planning department and development code.
claims.quotedLanguage: The Planning & Zoning Department's primary responsibility is to oversee and guide growth and development within the City. Staff administers the Unified Development Code and other City Ordinances pertaining to land use.
claims.notes: ⚠️ THIS IS A CORRECTNESS CLAIM, NOT A DIFFERENTIATION CLAIM. It is true of all six cities in the same way, so it cannot justify six separate pages. Quoted language is Star's; Boise's PDS page is the corroborating source. Meridian's site returns 403 to automated fetch and its page has NOT been read — do not quote Meridian.

claims.claim: In the City of Star, development within certain flood zones requires a Flood Plain Development Permit and must meet the City's Flood Hazard Ordinance; being in a flood zone does not by itself prevent obtaining a building permit.
claims.quotedLanguage: Development within certain flood zones requires a Flood Plain Development Permit and must meet the requirements of the City's Flood Hazard Ordinance.
claims.notes: RESOLVED — the answer was on Star's separate FAQ page, not the Planning & Zoning page. Star also directs owners to make an appointment with the planning department to have a property evaluated for flood zone location, rather than self-determining it.

claims.claim: Settlers Irrigation District delivers irrigation water to 13,187 acres of agricultural and urban land in western Ada County — the West Boise, Meridian and South Eagle areas — via a 20-mile canal and 95 miles of laterals.
claims.quotedLanguage: Settlers Irrigation District continues to deliver irrigation water to 13,187 acres of both agricultural and urban lands located in West Boise, Meridian, and South Eagle areas.
claims.notes: DIFFERENTIATING: this district covers PART of Boise, Meridian and Eagle — not all of any of them, and not Kuna, Star or Garden City. Never say 'Boise is in Settlers Irrigation District'; say West Boise. The district's own stated boundary is: Diversion Dam at Ann Morrison Park on the east, south to Franklin Road, west to Star Road, north to the Lower Bench.

claims.claim: The Boise Project Board of Control is the operating agent for five irrigation districts — Boise-Kuna, Big Bend, Nampa & Meridian, New York and Wilder — managing facilities transferred from the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation and delivering water to their landowners.
claims.quotedLanguage: Boise Project Board of Control is the operating agent for five irrigation districts: Boise-Kuna Irrigation District, Big Bend Irrigation District, Nampa & Meridian Irrigation District, New York Irrigation District, and Wilder Irrigation District.
claims.notes: Explains why 'who is my irrigation district' has a different answer across Ada County: Boise-Kuna, Nampa & Meridian and Settlers are separate entities serving different ground. The Board of Control is the OPERATING AGENT, not the district itself — do not conflate them.

claims.claim: Title to the Boise Project's transferred works — including Diversion Dam, the New York Canal, the Lake Lowell embankments and roughly 1,500 miles of canals, laterals and drains — remains in the United States.
claims.quotedLanguage: These facilities are referred to as "transferred works" and include all of the facilities beginning at Diversion Dam on the Boise River, and including the New York Canal, the embankments at Lake Lowell and approximately 1500 miles of canals, laterals, and drains. Title to the "transferred works" remains in the United States.
claims.notes: Materially seller-relevant and almost never stated on competitor sites: a canal or lateral crossing an Ada County parcel can sit on works whose title is FEDERAL, which changes who a landowner must deal with about encroachment, access and easements. Do not extrapolate this to every ditch — it applies to the transferred works named in the quote.

claims.claim: Ada County's own irrigation districts map identifies 27 separate irrigation entities operating in the county — irrigation districts, ditch companies, lateral associations, water companies and a drainage district — plus the Boise Project Board of Control as operating agent.
enumeration: Drain District No. 4 of Ada County
South Boise Mutual Irrigation Co LTD
claims.notes: Read from the county's published PDF map (cached at data/idaho/raw/pdf/ada-irrigation-districts.pdf, text extracted with pdftotext). This is INFORMATION GAIN of the strongest kind: 'which of Ada County's 27 irrigation entities serves this parcel' is a real question with a real answer that no competitor cash-buyer site addresses. ⚠️ The map shows WHICH entities exist and roughly where; it is a map, not a parcel lookup. Never state which entity serves a specific address from this source. The count is of named entities on the legend and excludes the Boise Project Board of Control, which is an operating agent for five of the districts rather than a district itself.

claims.claim: Ada County uses Areas of City Impact — unincorporated land planned in conjunction with an adjacent city. 78.8% of unincorporated Ada County residents (about 50,143 people) live inside an ACI, and only about 13,467 people, 2.4% of the county, live outside any ACI.
claims.quotedLanguage: Of those living in unincorporated Ada County, 78.8% (50,143) are estimated to live within an Area of City Impact (ACI). Only approximately 13,467 people live in unincorporated areas of the County outside of ACIs
claims.notes: IDAHO-SPECIFIC CONCEPT with no California analogue and real consequences for a seller: land in an ACI is unincorporated (county jurisdiction today) but planned with a city and a likely future annexation target. An ACI's population EXCEEDS its city's — Boise city 250,060 against Boise ACI 284,860.

claims.claim: Most Ada County residents living outside any Area of City Impact are in the planned communities of Avimor, Cartwright Ranch, Dry Creek Ranch and Hidden Springs.
claims.quotedLanguage: with many of these residents living in the planned communities of Avimor, Cartwright Ranch, Dry Creek Ranch and Hidden Springs.
claims.notes: ⚠️ NAMING CONFLICT: Ada County writes 'Hidden Springs'; the Census place-to-county file records 'Hidden Spring CDP' (singular). Use the county's spelling in prose about the community and the Census spelling when citing Census geography, and never present them as two places. These four are genuine unincorporated-county property markets, each on county jurisdiction for planning and permitting.

claims.claim: COMPASS projects Ada County will reach 715,820 by 2050, but the growth is projected to be very unevenly distributed: Kuna +128.7%, Eagle +50.6%, Garden City +42.0%, Meridian +34.8%, Boise +25.8%, Star +12.3%, while unincorporated Ada County is projected to LOSE 36.0% of its population.
claims.quotedLanguage: Unincorporated Ada County is projected to see a decrease of 22,920 residents by 2050, based on the assumption the cities will have annexed all of the area within their current ACI boundaries by that time.
claims.notes: ⚠️ A PROJECTION, not an estimate — must always be labelled as such, with the annexation assumption stated. The unincorporated DECLINE is not depopulation; it is the assumption that cities annex their ACIs. STRONG DIFFERENTIATOR and a genuine reversal: Star grew 1,009.7% since 2000 but is projected to add only 12.3% more by 2050, while Kuna is projected to more than double.

claims.claim: Median age varies sharply across Ada County's cities: Kuna 30.2, Boise 37.9, Meridian 38.7, Star 41.4, Eagle 46.8 and Garden City 47.1, against a county median of 39.1 (2022).
claims.notes: STRONGEST PER-CITY DIFFERENTIATOR FOUND SO FAR, and directly relevant to a property buyer: a 17-year spread between Kuna and Garden City implies materially different housing stock, tenure and life-stage mix. Ada County cites 2022 ACS; the figures were NOT read from ACS directly, hence MEDIUM confidence. Verify against ACS before making them load-bearing.

claims.claim: Ada County comprises six incorporated cities — Boise, Meridian, Eagle, Kuna, Star and Garden City — plus unincorporated county; 88.6% of residents live in one of the six cities and 11.4% live in unincorporated areas.
claims.quotedLanguage: According to COMPASS estimates, Ada County's population reached 557,590 in 2024, with the majority (88.6%) living in one of the County's six cities.
claims.notes: Six-city composition independently confirmed by the Census place-to-county relationship file, which also records Hidden Spring CDP as the county's only census-designated place and Star as spanning Ada and Canyon counties.

claims.claim: The City of Boise has a Wildland Urban Interface Overlay (WUI-O) zoning district covering land at higher risk of wildland fire, whose provisions apply to all new structures and additions built after its effective date and to renovations that increase a structure's gross floor area by more than 49 percent.
claims.quotedLanguage: The purpose of the WUI-O is to reduce the risks to human life, property, livelihoods, and wildlife within areas with higher risk of wildfire, and to recognize and clarify the respective roles of the city and property owners in the WUI-O to reduce those risks. ... The provisions of this Section 11-02-07.3.H shall apply to the following activities ... i. All new structures and additions to structures constructed in the WUI-O after the Effective Date; and ii. Renovation or modification of primary and accessory structures existing on the Effective Date that increase the gross floor area of the structure on the Effective Date by more than 49 percent.
claims.notes: GENUINE BOISE-ONLY DIFFERENTIATOR and directly material to a seller of a foothills property: a buyer planning to expand a WUI-O house by more than 49% of its gross floor area triggers the overlay's construction requirements. Interior-only renovations are excepted regardless of area. ⚠️ Do NOT assert that other Ada cities have or lack an equivalent overlay — not researched.

claims.claim: Boise participates in the National Flood Insurance Program because of significant flood threats from the Boise River, foothills gulches and several intermittent stream channels on the upper bench.
claims.quotedLanguage: The City of Boise participates in the National Flood Insurance Program due to the existence of significant flood threats related to the Boise River, foothills gulches and several intermittent stream channels on the upper bench.
claims.notes: Boise's flood exposure has THREE distinct sources, not just the river. Foothills gulches and upper-bench intermittent channels affect properties nowhere near the Boise River — a useful correction to the assumption that only riverfront property floods.

claims.claim: Any development within the floodplain in Ada County requires a Floodplain Development Permit, and the technical definition of floodplain for development purposes is in Ada County Ordinance 835.
claims.quotedLanguage: Any development within the Floodplain will require a Floodplain Development Permit.
claims.notes: Ada County calls these Hazardous Overlay Districts and administers them through its Engineering & Surveying Division. ⚠️ Ordinance 835 has NOT been read; cite it as the county names it, do not quote its contents.

claims.claim: Ada County adopted new FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Maps in June 2020.
claims.quotedLanguage: In June, 2020, Ada County adopted the new FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Maps.
claims.notes: ⚠️ DATE-SENSITIVE. Maps adopted 2020 may since have been revised. Re-verify before publishing, and never state a property's flood zone from any source but the current FEMA map for that address.

claims.claim: In the City of Star an original parcel may be divided one time administratively into no more than two lots, parcels or sites, without a public hearing, unless the City requires the applicant to plat the division.
claims.quotedLanguage: An original parcel of land may be divided one time, administratively, into not more than two (2) lots, parcels, or sites for transfer of ownership or development. This process does not require a public hearing, unless the City requires the applicant to plat the land division.
claims.notes: STAR-SPECIFIC DIFFERENTIATOR, directly useful to a land seller: a one-time, two-lot administrative split with no public hearing is a materially cheaper and faster path than a plat. ⚠️ This is STAR'S rule. Do not generalise it to the other five cities or to unincorporated Ada County — each has its own code and none has been checked.

claims.claim: The City of Star permits temporary living quarters in some cases to house an immediate family member where justified by health, employment or upkeep of the property; the structure may be permitted for two years and may not remain more than six years.
claims.quotedLanguage: Temporary living quarters are permitted in the City, in some cases, to house a member of the immediate family. The need for temporary living quarters for a family member must be justified for reasons of health, employment, or upkeep on the property. The structure may be permitted for two years and may not remain for more than six years.
claims.notes: Relevant to the manufactured-housing pillar and to inherited-property situations where a family member's unit sits on the parcel. Star-specific; not checked elsewhere.

claims.claim: Ada County Code Enforcement investigates land use and building code complaints in unincorporated Ada County only, and expressly does not enforce code violations within city limits; complainants remain anonymous.
claims.quotedLanguage: Ada County Code Enforcement does not enforce code violations within city limits. Please contact the municipal agency directly. ... A Code Enforcement Specialist will investigate written and verbal complaints concerning land use and building code issues in unincorporated Ada County. ... The complaining party will remain anonymous.
claims.notes: Directly relevant to the code-violations seller situation and reinforces the county/city split. The specialist is overseen by the Planning and Zoning Administrator in Development Services, and enforcement runs to civil District Court proceedings which can include fines, fees, penalties and in some instances incarceration. ⚠️ Never tell a seller inside a city to call Ada County about a violation.

claims.claim: The Ada County Assessor maintains comprehensive property records on all real and personal property in the county — parcel ownership, land and improvement characteristics, parcel boundaries and road rights-of-way — and manages the addressing process for all parcels in the county. Its online maps carry parcel boundaries, streets, hydrography, section boundaries, city limits, parks and schools, alongside Records of Survey and subdivision plats.
claims.quotedLanguage: The Ada County Assessor's Office maintains comprehensive property records on all real and personal property within the county. This includes, parcel ownership, land and improvement characteristics, parcel boundaries, road rights-of-way, and the office also manages the addressing processes for all parcels within the county.
claims.notes: Closes the GIS/parcel-records jurisdiction question: it is the ASSESSOR, not a separate GIS department, and the Assessor also owns ADDRESSING county-wide. Records of Survey and subdivision plats are available here, which matters for the land and difficult-property pillars.

claims.claim: The City of Eagle's Planning and Zoning Department administers the Eagle Zoning Ordinance, the Land Subdivision Ordinance, the Flood Control Ordinance and the Comprehensive Plan, and works with ACHD, COMPASS and the Idaho Transportation Department on transportation.
claims.quotedLanguage: It is the responsibility of the Planning and Zoning Department to provide for the administration of the City of Eagle Zoning Ordinance, the Land Subdivision Ordinance, the Flood Control Ordinance, and the Comprehensive Plan.
claims.notes: Eagle maintains a distinct FLOOD CONTROL ORDINANCE administered by its planning department — a named instrument the other cities' pages do not advertise, consistent with Eagle's position on the Boise River. Also independently corroborates ACHD as the road authority Eagle coordinates with, alongside COMPASS and ITD.

claims.claim: Garden City's Planning Division handles land use entitlements including annexation, zoning, conditional use permits, design review, signage and subdivisions.
claims.quotedLanguage: The Planning Division provides a wide variety of planning services for Garden City. Our services include, but are not limited to, land use entitlements such as Annexation, Zoning, Conditional Use Permits, Design Review, Signage, and Subdivisions.
claims.notes: Annexation is listed first among Garden City's entitlements, which is notable for a small city enclosed by Boise. Not yet a differentiator on its own — needs pairing with Garden City's distinctive median age of 47.1, the oldest in the county.

claims.claim: When an Idaho rental property changes ownership during a tenancy, the new owner becomes liable for refunding the tenant's security deposits.
claims.quotedLanguage: If security deposits have been made as to a particular rental or lease property, and the property changes ownership during a tenancy, the new owner shall be liable for refund of the deposits.
claims.notes: THE core statutory fact for the selling-with-tenants pillar, and it cuts both ways: a seller does not escape the deposit by selling, and a buyer inherits the refund liability. Directly relevant to our own acquisitions. ⚠️ This addresses DEPOSITS only. It says nothing about whether a lease itself survives a sale — that question is NOT answered by this section and must not be inferred from it.

claims.claim: An Idaho security deposit refund is due within 21 days if no time is fixed by agreement, and in any event within 30 days after the tenant surrenders the premises; any partial refund must be accompanied by a signed itemised statement.
claims.quotedLanguage: Refunds shall be made within twenty-one (21) days if no time is fixed by agreement and, in any event, within thirty (30) days after surrender of the premises by the tenant. Any refunds in an amount less than the full amount deposited by the tenant shall be accompanied by a signed statement itemizing the amounts lawfully retained by the landlord, the purpose for the amounts retained, and a detailed list of expenditures made from the deposit.

claims.claim: An Idaho landlord may not retain any part of a security deposit to cover normal wear and tear, defined as deterioration from the use the unit is intended for, without negligence, carelessness, accident, misuse or abuse.
claims.quotedLanguage: The landlord shall not retain any part of a security deposit to cover normal wear and tear. "Normal wear and tear" means that deterioration which occurs based upon the use for which the rental unit is intended and without negligence, carelessness, accident, or misuse or abuse of the premises or contents by the tenant or members of his household, or their invitees or guests.
claims.notes: Useful for the unwanted-rental and bad-tenants pages: a landlord selling a tired unit cannot charge the tenant for its condition where that condition is ordinary use.

claims.claim: If Idaho real property with a delinquency is not redeemed within three years from the date of delinquency, the county tax collector must issue a tax deed in favour of the county — but only after a notice of pending issue of tax deed has been given and an affidavit of compliance recorded.
claims.quotedLanguage: If real property on which there is a delinquency is not redeemed within three (3) years from the date of delinquency, the county tax collector of the county wherein such property is situated must make, in favor of said county, a tax deed for such property. However, the county shall not be entitled to a tax deed for such real property until: (a) A notice of pending issue of tax deed has been given; and (b) An affidavit of compliance has been recorded.
claims.notes: ⚠️⚠️ NEVER CONFLATE WITH MORTGAGE FORECLOSURE. Idaho's two routes to losing a property run on completely different clocks: a trust deed foreclosure needs 120 days' notice (45-1506), whereas property-tax delinquency takes THREE YEARS before a tax deed can even issue. A distressed seller who has heard '120 days' about one and applies it to the other will make a serious decision on a wrong timeline. This distinction is the core of the tax-delinquency pillar.

claims.claim: Notice of a pending Idaho tax deed must be served on record owners and parties in interest by certified mail with return receipt, no more than five months and no less than two months before the tax deed is set to issue; if returned undelivered, by publication once a week for four consecutive weeks, the last no more than two months and no less than fourteen days before issuance.
claims.quotedLanguage: By serving or causing to be served a copy of such notice by certified mail with return receipt demanded upon the record owner or owners and parties in interest of record at their last known address, such service of notice to be made no more than five (5) months nor less than two (2) months before the time set for the tax deed to issue;
claims.notes: The statute calls this the EXCLUSIVE manner of service. Owners and parties in interest are liable for the costs and fees of preparing, serving and publishing the notice.

claims.claim: After an Idaho tax deed issues to the county, the record owner or a party in interest may still redeem — but only until the county commissioners enter a contract of sale or transfer the property by county deed, and in any event the right expires fourteen months from the date the tax deed issued.
claims.quotedLanguage: such right of redemption shall expire fourteen (14) months from the date of issuance of a tax deed to the county, in the event the county commissioners have not extinguished the right of redemption by contract of sale or transfer by county deed during said redemption period.
claims.notes: ⚠️ DOUBLE-GATED, and both gates matter. The 14 months is a CEILING, not a guarantee: the right dies EARLIER if the county contracts to sell or conveys by county deed. Writing 'you have 14 months to redeem' without the earlier cut-off would tell an owner they have time they may not have. This mirrors the Missouri redemption trap on MoKan, where a headline period concealed the conditions that actually control it. Redemption requires paying the delinquency plus late charges, accrued interest and costs including title search and professional fees.

claims.claim: An Idaho manufactured home may constitute real property only if the running gear is removed, the home becomes permanently affixed to a foundation on land the owner owns or is purchasing (or leases under qualifying financing), and the owner records a statement of intent to declare it real property with the county recorder.
claims.quotedLanguage: A manufactured home may constitute real property if the running gear is removed and: (a) If the manufactured home becomes permanently affixed to a foundation: (i) On land which is owned or being purchased by the owner or purchaser of said manufactured home ... and (b) If the owner or purchaser of a manufactured home records with the county recorder in the county in which the manufactured home will be situated a statement of intent to declare the manufactured home as real property.
claims.notes: ⚠️ ALL THREE CONDITIONS ARE REQUIRED — running gear removed, permanently affixed on qualifying land, AND a recorded statement of intent. A manufactured home sitting on owned land with the axles gone is still PERSONAL PROPERTY if nothing was recorded. This is the single most consequential fact for a manufactured-home seller: it decides whether the home conveys by deed or by title, and whether it is even part of the real estate being sold. Connects directly to the Ada County Assessor's three-factor fixture test (annexation, adaptation, intent).

claims.claim: Once an Idaho manufactured home has been declared real property, county assessors must treat it as any other site-built residence, and lending institutions are permitted to treat it as real property.
claims.quotedLanguage: The exercise of said option shall require all county assessors to treat those manufactured homes whose owners or purchasers have exercised said option as any other site-built residence and shall permit lending institutions to treat said manufactured homes as real property or as any other residence.
claims.notes: Explains the practical stakes for a seller: conversion changes both how the home is assessed and whether conventional real-property financing is available to a buyer — which changes the buyer pool. The declaration is REVERSIBLE under 63-305, and the form must have the certificate of origin or original title attached to permit that reversal.

claims.claim: Idaho provides a limited alternative remedy allowing a residential property owner or authorized agent to request that the county sheriff immediately remove persons unlawfully occupying a residential dwelling, subject to eight cumulative conditions.
claims.quotedLanguage: A property owner or the owner's authorized agent may request from the sheriff of the county in which the property is located the immediate removal of a person or persons unlawfully occupying a residential dwelling pursuant to this section if all of the following conditions are met: (a) The requesting person is the property owner or authorized agent ... (f) The unauthorized person or persons are not current or former tenants pursuant to a written or oral rental agreement authorized by the property owner; (g) The unauthorized person or persons are not immediate family members of the property owner; and (h) There is no pending litigation related to the real property between the property owner and any known unauthorized person.
claims.notes: ⚠️⚠️ ALL EIGHT CONDITIONS MUST BE MET, and three of them exclude the situations sellers most often describe as 'squatters': a current OR FORMER TENANT under a written or oral agreement is excluded (f), an immediate family member is excluded (g), and any pending litigation over the property excludes it (h). This remedy is for genuine unlawful entry, NOT for a holdover tenant or a relative who will not leave — those go through ordinary eviction. Never present 6-310A as a fast route around eviction. Requires a completed and verified 'Complaint to Remove Persons Unlawfully Occupying Residential Real Property' submitted to the sheriff. This section is informational only and is not legal advice.

claims.claim: In August 2025 the City of Meridian issued 103 new residential building permits with a stated total valuation of $23,900,907.90, and 10 new commercial permits valued at $35,391,436.00; commercial permits of all types totalled 77 permits at $67,132,621.00.
claims.quotedLanguage: New TOTAL VALUE: $23,900,907.90 103 PERMITS ... New TOTAL VALUE: $35,391,436.00 10 PERMITS ... COMMERCIAL TOTAL $67,132,621.00 77 PERMITS
claims.notes: FIRST MERIDIAN-SOURCED CLAIM. meridiancity.org returns 403 to automated HTML fetches but serves its PDF assets normally, which is how this was obtained. ⚠️ SINGLE MONTH, AUGUST 2025 — a snapshot, not a trend, and it must always be labelled with its month and year. The residential/commercial attribution was verified against the report's own section headers rather than inferred from the figures. No residential grand total is stated in the report and none is asserted here.

claims.claim: The City of Kuna assigns a zone to every property within city limits, and Kuna Municipal Code 5-3-2 holds the Official Land Use Table: uses marked 'P' are permitted, 'S' requires a Special Use Permit, and a use not listed is prohibited in that zone.
claims.quotedLanguage: The City of Kuna has assigned a zone to every property located within Kuna city limits. ... you may view 5-3-2 of the Kuna Municipal Code which contains the Official Land Use Table. This will show the uses allowed in each zoning district. Uses are listed as "P" for a Permitted Use and "S" signifying by Special Use Permit only. If none of these are listed, the use is prohibited in that zone.
claims.notes: The 'not listed means prohibited' convention is the useful part for a seller weighing what a buyer could do with a Kuna parcel — it is a closed-list code, not a permissive one. ⚠️ Kuna's convention; do not generalise to the other cities.

claims.claim: Kuna notifies property owners within 300 feet of a subject property of a public hearing, in writing, at least fifteen days before the hearing.
claims.quotedLanguage: Notification for public hearings is 300' from the subject property. Written notification is then mailed at least fifteen (15) days prior to the public hearing.
claims.notes: Concrete Kuna-specific procedural fact. Relevant to a seller whose neighbour is seeking a rezone, and to a buyer planning an entitlement.

claims.claim: Kuna advises that the best way to determine property lines is a professional survey, that owners should check for existing corner pins or stakes, that the Ada County Assessor's Office may hold a copy showing property size and surrounding lots, and that fence lines and street curbs should not be assumed to follow property lines.
claims.quotedLanguage: Do not assume that fence lines and street curbs follow property lines.
claims.notes: Useful for the boundary-dispute and difficult-property pillars, and it routes back to the Assessor, which the registry already establishes as the holder of parcel boundaries and Records of Survey.

claims.claim: Under Idaho's recording act, every conveyance of real property OTHER THAN a lease for a term not exceeding one year is void as against a subsequent purchaser or mortgagee in good faith and for valuable consideration whose conveyance is first duly recorded.
claims.quotedLanguage: Every conveyance of real property other than a lease for a term not exceeding one (1) year, is void as against any subsequent purchaser or mortgagee of the same property, or any part thereof, in good faith and for a valuable consideration, whose conveyance is first duly recorded.
claims.notes: ⚠️⚠️ THIS IS THE STATUTORY MECHANISM, NOT A LEGAL CONCLUSION ABOUT ANY PARTICULAR LEASE. What the statute says: a lease for a term of ONE YEAR OR LESS is carved OUT of the voiding rule, so it is not void against a later purchaser merely for being unrecorded. A lease LONGER than one year that is unrecorded falls inside the rule and may be void against a subsequent purchaser who takes in good faith, for value, and records first. Whether a specific lease binds a specific buyer turns on facts this section does not resolve — notably whether the purchaser took in GOOD FAITH, which can be affected by a tenant's visible possession. Idaho Code 55-606 states the parallel rule for grants generally. NEVER write 'a lease always survives a sale in Idaho' or 'a buyer can always terminate an unrecorded lease'. State the rule, name the one-year carve-out, and direct the reader to counsel for their own lease. This is the answer to the open lease-survival question insofar as statute answers it.

claims.claim: Residential and commercial buildings in Boise must connect to the city sewer system, which the Public Works Department operates across more than 1,000 miles of pipe.
claims.quotedLanguage: Residential and commercial buildings must connect to the sewer system.
claims.notes: THE CITY/COUNTY UTILITY CONTRAST IN ONE FACT: inside Boise, connection to city sewer is mandatory; in unincorporated Ada County, on-site septic is permitted by Central District Health. A seller's answer to 'what happens to waste water here' depends entirely on which side of the city limit the parcel sits.

claims.claim: Boise charges a one-time sewer assessment fee, separate from connection fees, for properties that have never been developed or never connected; it is likely to apply when building on a lot being split, building on a previously undeveloped lot, or connecting an existing building to sanitary sewer.
claims.quotedLanguage: If you are building on an existing lot which is being split, building on a previously undeveloped lot or connecting an existing building to sanitary sewer, the assessment component of the connection fees will likely be required.
claims.notes: DIRECTLY MATERIAL TO AN INFILL-LOT OR LOT-SPLIT SELLER IN BOISE: a buyer's cost is not just the connection fee but a separate assessment fee, and the city names lot splits and previously undeveloped lots as the cases where it will likely apply. This is a real number in a buyer's calculation that a seller is often unaware of. ⚠️ The page states no amounts — do not publish a figure. Connection fees themselves comprise trunk fees and treatment fees, and the physical connection from building to right-of-way is NOT included in either.

claims.claim: Once an Idaho manufactured home has been converted to real property, it is deemed a fixture and an improvement to the land, and physically removing it is prohibited without the consent of every person or entity holding an interest in the real property or title to any estate in it. The homeowner must obtain a title report from a title insurance company to establish whose consent is required. Owners of rights-of-way, easements and subsurface rights are excluded from that requirement.
claims.quotedLanguage: Physical removal shall be prohibited without the consent of all persons or entities who, at the time of removal have an interest in the real property or title to any estate in the real property to which the manufactured home has been affixed.
claims.notes: 🎯 THE DECISIVE FACT FOR A SELLER, and the reason this subject deserves a page. Declaring a manufactured home real property under § 63-304 is a filing. Undoing it is not: it requires unanimous consent from everyone with an interest in the land, established by a title report the owner must pay for. It is a one-way door in practice even though the statute provides a route back. ⚠️ 'Physical removal' is defined broadly at § 63-305(2) to include separating the home from its foundation system, except temporarily for repair or improvement — so this reaches work an owner would not think of as removal.

claims.claim: An Idaho homeowner must give the county assessor at least thirty days' written notice before removing a manufactured home that has been converted to real property, and the assessor must require written evidence that the necessary consents have been obtained.
claims.quotedLanguage: At least thirty (30) days before the manufactured home is to be removed, the homeowner shall give written notice of the intended removal to the county assessor in the county in which the real property is located.
claims.notes: The procedural half of § 63-305. ⚠️ The statute continues past what is quoted here into a tax-collector condition on removal that has NOT been read in full — do not state anything about outstanding taxes and removal beyond the notice requirement until § 63-305(3) is read to its end.

claims.claim: Idaho requires manufactured homes to be assessed as other residential housing, with those assessments entered on the property roll.
claims.quotedLanguage: Manufactured homes shall be assessed as other residential housing and such assessments shall be entered on the property roll.
claims.notes: ⚠️ MEDIUM AND EASY TO OVER-READ. The section is a single sentence about ASSESSMENT METHOD. It does not say a manufactured home IS real property — that is § 63-304 and it has conditions. Never cite this as evidence that the real/personal distinction does not matter; it says how the value is worked out, not what the thing legally is.

claims.claim: Boise no longer requires a short-term rental license. The City Council approved repeal of the city's short-term rental ordinance on May 12, 2026, to align with changes in Idaho state law on local regulation of short-term rentals, effective May 18, 2026. The city says it will continue enforcing nuisance, noise, parking, safety and occupancy rules.
claims.quotedLanguage: On May 12, 2026, Boise City Council approved the repeal of the city’s short-term rental ordinance to align with changes in Idaho state law regarding local regulation of short-term rentals.
claims.notes: Materially useful to anyone buying or selling a Boise property with short-term rental income in mind, and very recent. ⚠️ VOLATILE: it follows a state law change, and further legislation could move it again. ⚠️ Repeal of the LICENSE is not repeal of every rule — the city states it still enforces nuisance, noise, parking, safety and occupancy regulations. Never write that short-term rentals are unregulated in Boise. ⚠️ The state law change itself has not been read; do not describe it.

claims.claim: Boise charges development impact fees that differ by type of development: new residential development pays parks, fire and police impact fees, while commercial development pays only fire and police fees because it typically does not directly impact regional and local parks.
claims.quotedLanguage: New residential development pays parks, fire, and police impact fee types because they impact all three services. Commercial development pays only fire and police impact fees, because it typically does not directly impact regional and local parks.
claims.notes: ⚠️ No fee AMOUNT is claimed. The schedule is a separate document that was not read, and amounts change on update — the city's study is revised every five years.

claims.claim: Boise exempts several activities from impact fees, including replacing a residential unit — a manufactured home included — with another residential unit on the same lot where the number of service units does not increase, remodeling that does not add service units, and rebuilding the same floor area after a fire or other catastrophe if it is ready for occupancy within two years.
claims.quotedLanguage: Replacing a residential unit, including a manufactured home, with another residential unit on the same lot, provided that the number of service units does not increase
claims.notes: The seller-relevant point is the line between replacing and adding: a buyer who replaces a house one-for-one avoids impact fees, and one who adds units pays them. ⚠️ Council-approved exemptions as the city lists them; the underlying code section was not read. Do not describe an exemption more broadly than the city's wording.

claims.claim: Boise replaced its zoning code with a modern zoning code approved by the City Council and effective December 1, 2023, so zoning rules for a Boise parcel may differ from what applied before that date.
claims.quotedLanguage: A similar process was followed by Boise City Council, hearing community testimony, advising revisions and approving the zoning code effective December 1, 2023.
claims.notes: Useful because owners often carry an old understanding of what their lot allows. ⚠️ Says nothing about WHAT changed for any district or parcel — only that the code was replaced and when. The dimensional claims elsewhere in this project are read from the current codified text.

claims.claim: Boise's demolition and deconstruction permit application includes a material and waste management plan with photos of the building and its materials; the city emails reuse and recycling companies about available materials and allows up to five business days for them to respond before salvage is arranged. A building inspector sets a bond, and hazardous materials must be abated under applicable EPA and other requirements.
claims.quotedLanguage: Allow up to five (5) business days for response of interest in any materials from Reuse Companies.
claims.notes: Relevant to anyone selling a teardown or buying one: demolition in Boise is a permitted process with a bond and a built-in reuse step, not a same-week job. ⚠️ Bond amounts are set case by case by the inspector and are not claimed.

claims.claim: Boise has ten designated historic districts: six residential (East End, East Main Street, Harrison Boulevard, Hays Street, North End and Warm Springs Avenue), three commercial (Hyde Park, Old Boise and South Eighth Street) and one agricultural (Spaulding Ranch).
claims.quotedLanguage: Boise has ten designated historic districts that serve as visible reminders of the historical, archaeological, architectural, educational, and cultural heritage of Boise.
claims.notes: ⚠️ District boundaries are not claimed — the city provides an address lookup, and whether a given parcel is inside a district must be checked there, never inferred from a neighbourhood name. 'North End' as people use it and the North End Historic District are not necessarily the same area.

claims.claim: In Boise's historic districts, most exterior changes beyond standard maintenance require a Certificate of Appropriateness — including new construction, additions, accessory buildings, and changes such as siding and windows — with the level of review set by a decision matrix based on the district, the property's status and the scope of work.
claims.quotedLanguage: Most exterior changes in the historic districts require a Certificate of Appropriateness to make modifications to a home in a Historic District outside of standard maintenance
claims.notes: The practical point for a seller: a buyer planning to replace windows or re-side a house in a Boise historic district is buying a review process, not just a project. ⚠️ 'Most', not all — the decision matrix decides, and the level of review varies. Never write that every change requires one.

claims.claim: In Star, water and sewer service is provided by the Star Sewer & Water District, a separate entity from the City of Star.
claims.quotedLanguage: Star Sewer & Water District
claims.notes: Useful because owners assume the city runs water and sewer, and a service, connection or billing question in Star goes to the district instead. ⚠️ The city's page LISTS the district as the water and sewer provider; the district's own boundaries and whether it serves every Star parcel were not read.

claims.claim: The City of Star requires building permits for, among other things, re-roofing, replacing more than 100 square feet of siding, replacing windows or doors where the openings are enlarged or reduced, decks 30 or more inches above grade, sheds or outbuildings of 200 square feet or larger, fences over 6 feet, retaining walls over 4 feet, setting manufactured homes, and demolition. No building permit is required for a concrete slab.
claims.quotedLanguage: Replacement of windows or doors where the openings are enlarged or reduced
claims.notes: The seller-relevant use is unpermitted work: a re-roof or deck done without a permit in Star is a finding a buyer's inspector or lender may raise. ⚠️ Star's list only. Boise and the other cities have their own triggers; do not generalise.

claims.claim: In Star a homeowner who pulls a building permit must perform all the work on it, may pull permits on a primary or secondary residence without registering as a contractor with the state, and must plan on living in the residence within 12 months of completing the project; otherwise a licensed contractor must pull the permit.
claims.quotedLanguage: Homeowners can pull permits on their primary or secondary residence without registering as a contractor with the state and must plan on living in the residence within 12 months of completion of the project.
claims.notes: Directly relevant to flips and pre-sale repairs: an owner fixing up a Star house to sell, rather than to live in, does not fit the homeowner-permit route as the city describes it. ⚠️ Do not state a penalty or consequence; none is described.

claims.claim: The City of Star notes that a Certificate of Occupancy names the municipality actually responsible for permitting and inspection, which can differ from the city associated with the property's ZIP code, because ZIP codes are managed by the Postal Service for mail delivery and do not follow municipal boundaries.
claims.quotedLanguage: ZIP codes are created and managed by the United States Postal Service for mail delivery purposes and do not reflect municipal boundaries.
claims.notes: A genuine trap in a fast-growing edge city: a mailing address that says one city does not settle which city's code governs the parcel. ⚠️ The general ZIP-versus-boundary point is true everywhere, but this claim is the City of Star saying it about its own certificates; attribute it that way.

claims.claim: Drinking water in Boise is supplied by privately owned utilities regulated by the Idaho Public Utilities Commission, chiefly Veolia Water Idaho and Capitol Water Corporation. Both bill their customers inside Boise city limits a 3 percent City of Boise franchise fee — for Veolia under City of Boise Ordinance No. 5623, effective December 17, 2003.
claims.quotedLanguage: City of Boise 5623 December 17, 2003 3.0%
claims.notes: 🎯 Resolves an open question recorded 2026-09-12: who supplies Boise's drinking water. The city's own 'water future' page is about WASTEWATER and names no supplier, which is why this was withheld until primary sources were found. The strongest evidence is the franchise fee: Veolia's Commission-approved tariff bills it 'to its customers within the corporate limits of a municipality', and Capitol Water's service agreement collects '3% of customer basic charges for the City of Boise Franchise Fees' — so both demonstrably serve inside city limits. ⚠️ Worded affirmatively on purpose. Do NOT state that 'the city does not supply any drinking water' as a fact — that is a negative claim, and this project has learned those are traps. ⚠️ 'Chiefly', not 'only': EPA records list many small private community systems (homeowners associations, water associations, mobile home parks) with Boise addresses, and their service locations were not mapped. ⚠️ Third-party water-quality sites claiming Veolia serves Meridian and Kuna are NOT sources and conflict with those cities running their own systems — never cite them.

claims.claim: In 2023 the Idaho Public Utilities Commission described Veolia Water Idaho as providing service to Boise City and surrounding areas and serving approximately 105,000 customers in Ada County, under Amended Certificate of Public Convenience No. 143. The Commission's 2023 annual report lists Veolia Water Idaho at 105,445 customers and Capitol Water at 3,019, both with Boise as the nearest city.
claims.quotedLanguage: Veolia is a Commission-regulated water corporation that provides service to Boise City and surrounding areas and currently serves approximately 105,000 customers in Ada County, Idaho.
claims.notes: HISTORICAL because both figures are 2023 snapshots — the page labels it as a fixed past period so a dated count is never presented as current. The City of Boise was an intervenor in the same rate case. ⚠️ Veolia's customers are in Ada County, not all inside Boise city limits, so 105,000 is not a count of Boise households.

claims.claim: Veolia Water Idaho draws on both surface and ground water: the state's drinking water record lists two treatment plants, Columbia and Marden, alongside dozens of wells, and federal records classify the system's primary source as surface water and put it at 264,978 people served through 108,138 connections. The City of Boise, for its part, states that 70 percent of Boise's drinking water supply comes from groundwater.
claims.quotedLanguage: Principal County Served : ADA Primary Source : SW
claims.notes: ⚠️ These two statements look contradictory and are NOT presented as reconciled. A federal 'primary source: surface water' classification and a city statement that 70 percent of supply is groundwater measure different things, and neither source explains the other. State both, attributed, and never write that Boise's water is 'mostly surface water' or 'mostly groundwater' on this evidence. The well count is left as 'dozens' because it was counted from a listing page rather than stated.

claims.claim: Capitol Water Corporation, Boise's second regulated water utility, supplies groundwater: its 2025 water quality report describes water from four primary wells and one backup well, and federal records put the system at 9,000 people served through 2,811 connections.
claims.quotedLanguage: water from four primary wells and one
claims.notes: ⚠️ The same 2025 report discusses a water quality violation. It is deliberately not part of this claim: it is not relevant to which utility serves a property, and describing another business's compliance history on a property-buying site invites a characterisation this evidence does not support. Do not add it.

claims.claim: Veolia Water Idaho acquired Eagle Water Company, and its Commission-approved tariff keeps a separate General Metered Service schedule for the Eagle Water Service Area covering customers in the area formerly served by Eagle Water Company as of January 1, 2022. Veolia also bills a 1 percent City of Eagle franchise fee under Eagle Ordinance No. 414.
claims.quotedLanguage: All existing customers at time of acquisition in the area formerly serviced by Eagle Water Company
claims.notes: Useful to an Eagle seller or buyer because a property in the former Eagle Water Company area can sit on a different rate schedule from neighbouring Veolia customers. ⚠️ Rates themselves are not claimed; they change on the next rate order. ⚠️ The acquisition date is not stated in what was read — only the January 1, 2022 customer cutoff.

claims.claim: Water service in Eagle is split by area.
