claims.claim: On an application for informal probate, the registrar issues a written statement of informal probate once the required findings are made, if at least five days have passed since the death; informal probate is conclusive until superseded by an order in a formal testacy proceeding.
claims.quotedLanguage: the registrar, upon making the findings required by section 15-3-303 of this chapter shall issue a written statement of informal probate if at least five (5) days have elapsed since the decedent's death. Informal probate is conclusive as to all persons until superseded by an order in a formal testacy proceeding.
claims.notes: Five days is a statutory MINIMUM before the registrar may act, not a processing time. Never present it as how long probate takes. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: On an application for informal appointment, the registrar appoints the applicant, subject to qualification and acceptance, once at least 120 hours have passed since the death (delayed to 30 days for a nonresident decedent, with exceptions); informal appointment fully establishes the status, powers and duties of a personal representative.
claims.quotedLanguage: if at least one hundred twenty (120) hours have elapsed since the decedent's death, the registrar, after making the findings required by section 15-3-308 of this chapter, shall appoint the applicant subject to qualification and acceptance; provided, that if the decedent was a nonresident, the registrar shall delay the order of appointment until thirty (30) days have elapsed since death ... The status of personal representative and the powers and duties pertaining to the office are fully established by informal appointment.
claims.notes: 120 hours is a minimum, not a processing time. The nonresident 30-day delay has two exceptions (domiciliary PR is the applicant; will directs Idaho law) — say 'with exceptions' if the 30 days is mentioned. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: A formal testacy proceeding in Idaho is litigation to determine whether the decedent left a valid will. Once a previously appointed personal representative receives notice of one, they must refrain from further distribution while it is pending; a petitioner may ask the court to restrain the acting representative's powers, but absent such an order the proceeding affects only powers relating to distribution.
claims.quotedLanguage: A formal testacy proceeding is litigation to determine whether a decedent left a valid will. ... a previously appointed personal representative, after receipt of notice of the commencement of a formal probate proceeding, must refrain from exercising his power to make any further distribution of the estate during the pendency of the formal proceeding. A petitioner who seeks the appointment of a different personal representative in a formal proceeding also may request an order restraining the acting personal representative from exercising any of the powers of his office and requesting the appointment of a special administrator. In the absence of a request, or if the request is denied, the commencement of a formal proceeding has no effect on the powers and duties of a previously appointed personal representative other than those relating to distribution.
claims.notes: Do not say a will contest 'freezes' a sale. The statute freezes DISTRIBUTION; other powers continue unless a restraining order is sought and granted. Whether a given sale is wise during a contest is for the estate's attorney. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Supervised administration is a single proceeding under the continuing authority of the court; a supervised personal representative answers to the court and is subject to its directions, but otherwise has the same duties and powers as an unsupervised one.
claims.quotedLanguage: Supervised administration is a single in rem proceeding to secure complete administration and settlement of a decedent's estate under the continuing authority of the court ... A supervised personal representative is responsible to the court, as well as to the interested parties, and is subject to directions concerning the estate made by the court on its own motion or on the motion of any interested party.
claims.notes: Supervised administration is the exception to the 'no court order' default in 15-3-704. State it alongside pb-pr-proceeds-without-court-order. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: An Idaho personal representative must proceed expeditiously with settling and distributing the estate and, except where supervised administration provides otherwise, does so without adjudication, order or direction of the court, though they may invoke the court to resolve questions.
claims.quotedLanguage: A personal representative shall proceed expeditiously with the settlement and distribution of a decedent's estate and, except as otherwise specified or ordered in regard to a supervised personal representative, do so without adjudication, order, or direction of the court, but he may invoke the jurisdiction of the court, in proceedings authorized by this code, to resolve questions concerning the estate or its administration.
claims.notes: Must be stated with the supervised-administration exception and, wherever sale power is discussed, with id-pr-powers-limited-by-will. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Idaho sets a priority order for appointment as personal representative: the person with priority under a probated will; a surviving spouse who is a devisee; other devisees; the surviving spouse; other heirs; then, 45 days after death, any creditor; and if a petition has been filed and 60 days pass with no proper person consenting to act, the public administrator. Persons sharing a priority who do not renounce must concur in nominating someone or in applying.
claims.quotedLanguage: (a) Whether the proceedings are formal or informal, persons who are not disqualified have priority for appointment in the following order: (1) the person with priority as determined by a probated will including a person nominated by a power conferred in a will; (2) the surviving spouse of the decedent who is a devisee of the decedent; (3) other devisees of the decedent; (4) the surviving spouse of the decedent; (5) other heirs of the decedent; (6) forty-five (45) days after the death of the decedent, any creditor; (7) if a petition for appointment of a personal representative has been filed and sixty (60) days have elapsed during which no consent to act has been filed by any proper person, the public administrator shall act as personal representative unless and until a proper person consents to act. ... When two (2) or more persons share a priority, those of them who do not renounce must concur in nominating another to act for them, or in applying for appointment.
claims.notes: Pairs with ada-treasurer-ex-officio-public-administrator (the Ada Treasurer is the public administrator). The concurrence rule is what bites when several siblings share priority as heirs. Objections are only heard in formal proceedings (15-3-203(b)) — not separately claimed. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: To acquire the powers of a personal representative in Idaho, a person must be appointed by the court or registrar, qualify, and be issued letters; administration of an estate begins with the issuance of letters.
claims.quotedLanguage: Except as otherwise provided in chapter 4 of this code, to acquire the powers and undertake the duties and liabilities of a personal representative of a decedent, a person must be appointed by order of the court or registrar, qualify and be issued letters. Administration of an estate is commenced by the issuance of letters.
claims.notes: The basis for saying a named executor in a will has no power to sell until appointed and issued letters. 'Except as otherwise provided in chapter 4' refers to foreign personal representatives — not covered on the page. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Before receiving letters, an Idaho personal representative qualifies by filing any required bond and a statement of acceptance, including an oath to perform the duties of the office according to law.
claims.quotedLanguage: Prior to receiving letters, a personal representative shall qualify by filing with the appointing court any required bond and a statement of acceptance of the duties of the office. In his statement of acceptance, the personal representative shall subscribe an oath to the effect that he will perform the duties of his office according to the law.
claims.notes: 'Any required bond' — the page must not say a bond is always required. When one is required is not covered. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: A personal representative's duties and powers begin on appointment; the powers relate back to give beneficial acts done before appointment the same effect, and the representative may ratify proper acts done by others.
claims.quotedLanguage: Duties and powers of a personal representative commence upon his appointment. The powers of a personal representative relate back in time to give acts by the person appointed which are beneficial to the estate occurring prior to appointment the same effect as those occurring thereafter.
claims.notes: Relation-back is NOT an invitation to sign a purchase contract before appointment. The page should say only that powers start on appointment and leave pre-appointment acts to an attorney. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: On payment of the required fees, the Idaho court clerk must issue certified copies of probated wills, letters issued to personal representatives and other filed records; certificates relating to letters must show the date of appointment.
claims.quotedLanguage: Upon payment of the fees required by law the clerk must issue certified copies of any probated wills, letters issued to personal representatives, or any other record or paper filed or recorded. ... Certificates relating to letters must show the date of appointment.
claims.notes: This says what the CLERK must issue. It does NOT say what a title company requires; no primary source found says that. Do not write 'the title company will ask for certified letters dated within X days'. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Letters of a personal representative, a statement of informal probate, and any deed executed by an appointed personal representative, among other documents affecting title to real property, may be recorded with the county recorder where the property is, and from filing they give notice of their contents to everyone.
claims.quotedLanguage: Letters of personal representatives (foreign or domestic), a statement of informal probate, probated will, determination of heirship, order made in a testacy proceeding ... any deed, assignment, release or other instrument executed by an appointed personal representative of the decedent; an affidavit of a successor in interest to property of a decedent ... may be recorded in the office of the county recorder of the county in which the real property affected by any such letters, statement, determination, order, document or decree is located. From the time of filing the same for record, notice is imparted to all persons of the contents thereof.
claims.notes: 'MAY be recorded' — permissive. Do not say recording is required. Recording county = county where the PROPERTY is (contrast venue, which follows domicile). Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: A person who in good faith deals with an Idaho personal representative for value is protected as if the representative properly exercised the power, need not inquire into the existence or propriety of the power, and is bound by a will or court limitation on the representative's power only with actual knowledge of it — except for restrictions on supervised representatives endorsed on the letters, and without regard to recording-based constructive notice.
claims.quotedLanguage: A person who in good faith either assists a personal representative or deals with him for value is protected as if the personal representative properly exercised his power. The fact that a person knowingly deals with a personal representative does not alone require the person to inquire into the existence of a power or the propriety of its exercise. Except for restrictions on powers of supervised personal representatives which are endorsed on letters as provided in section 15-3-504 of this code, and without regard to the constructive notice provisions of section 15-1-305A of this code, no provision in any will or order of court purporting to limit the power of a personal representative is effective except as to persons with actual knowledge thereof.
claims.notes: ⚠️ This protects the BUYER, not the personal representative. Never present it as meaning the PR may ignore a will restriction (id-pr-powers-limited-by-will still binds the PR). Keep the endorsed-on-letters exception in any statement of it. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Among the transactions Idaho Code 15-3-715 authorises for a personal representative are acquiring or disposing of an asset, including land, at public or private sale, and selling, mortgaging or leasing any real property of the estate for cash or credit.
claims.quotedLanguage: (6) Acquire or dispose of an asset, including land in this or another state, for cash or on credit, at public or private sale; ... (23) Sell, mortgage, or lease any real or personal property of the estate or any interest therein for cash, credit, or for part cash and part credit, and with or without security for unpaid balances;
claims.notes: ⚠️ MUST BE STATED WITH id-pr-powers-limited-by-will — the same section's lead-in ('Except as restricted or otherwise provided by the will or by an order in a formal proceeding ... acting reasonably for the benefit of the interested persons'). History note copied from the cached 15-3-715 page (existing source; the existing claim id-pr-powers-limited-by-will carries no amendmentHistory). claims.claim: Unless the will provides otherwise, an Idaho personal representative has the right to take possession or control of the decedent's property, though real property may be left with the person presumptively entitled to it until the representative judges possession necessary for administration; the representative must pay taxes on, and take reasonable steps to manage, protect and preserve, the estate in their possession.
claims.quotedLanguage: Except as otherwise provided by a decedent's will, every personal representative has a right to, and shall take possession or control of, the decedent's property, except that any real property or tangible personal property may be left with or surrendered to the person presumptively entitled thereto unless or until, in the judgment of the personal representative, possession of the property by him will be necessary for purposes of administration. ... The personal representative shall pay taxes on, and take all steps reasonably necessary for the management, protection and preservation of, the estate in his possession.
claims.notes: Relevant to a vacant house during administration (taxes, insurance, upkeep). Do not convert into advice about a specific heir occupying the house. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: On appointment, an Idaho personal representative may publish a notice to creditors once a week for three successive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation in the county, requiring claims within four months of first publication or be forever barred; written notice to a known creditor sets a deadline of four months after publication or 60 days after mailing or delivery, whichever is later.
claims.quotedLanguage: (a) Unless notice has already been given under this section, a personal representative upon his appointment may publish a notice to creditors once a week for three (3) successive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation in the county announcing his appointment and address and notifying creditors of the estate to present their claims within four (4) months after the date of the first publication of the notice or be forever barred. (b) A personal representative may give written notice by mail or other delivery to any creditor, notifying the creditor to present his claim within four (4) months after the published notice if given as provided in subsection (a) of this section or within sixty (60) days after the mailing or delivery of the notice, whichever is later, or be forever barred.
claims.notes: 'MAY publish' — notice is permissive in the text, not mandatory (subsection (d) adds a medical-assistance notice duty for decedents 55+, not claimed here). Four months runs from FIRST publication. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Pre-death claims against an Idaho estate (other than state tax claims) are barred unless presented by the earlier of three years after death or the deadline set by a notice to creditors under 15-3-801; the section does not affect proceedings to enforce a mortgage or other lien on estate property.
claims.quotedLanguage: (a) All claims against a decedent's estate which arose before the death of the decedent, including claims of the state and any subdivision thereof (except claims for state taxes), whether due or to become due ... are barred against the estate, the personal representative, and the heirs and devisees of the decedent, unless presented within the earlier of the following dates: (1) three (3) years after the decedent's death; or (2) within the time provided in section 15-3-801 (b), Idaho Code, for creditors who are given actual notice, and within the time provided in section 15-3-801 (a), Idaho Code, for all creditors barred by publication. ... (e) Nothing in this section affects or prevents: (1) any proceeding to enforce any mortgage, pledge, or other lien upon property of the estate;
claims.notes: ⚠️ The (e)(1) carve-out is essential on a house page: a mortgage on the house is NOT cut off by the creditor deadline. State tax claims run on a separate clock (803(d)) — not covered. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Unless the court prohibits it, and outside supervised administration, an Idaho personal representative may close an estate by sworn statement filed no earlier than six months after the original appointment, stating among other things that the time for presenting creditors' claims has expired; if nothing is pending a year after filing, the appointment terminates.
claims.quotedLanguage: Unless prohibited by order of the court and except for estates being administered in supervised administration proceedings, a personal representative may close an estate by filing with the court no earlier than six (6) months after the date of original appointment of a general personal representative for the estate, a verified statement stating that he, or a previous personal representative whom he has succeeded, has or have: (1) determined that the time limitation for presentation of creditors' claims has expired; ... (b) If no proceedings involving the personal representative are pending in the court one (1) year after the closing statement is filed, the appointment of the personal representative terminates.
claims.notes: Six months is the earliest CLOSING by sworn statement — it is not a waiting period for a sale. Do not conflate. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Subject to listed exceptions, no informal or formal probate or appointment proceeding may be commenced in Idaho more than three years after the death; the limit does not apply to proceedings under 15-3-1201 or 15-3-1205, or to proceedings to construe probated wills or determine heirs of an intestate.
claims.quotedLanguage: may be commenced more than three (3) years after the decedent's death, except: ... These limitations do not apply to proceedings to construe probated wills or determine heirs of an intestate or to proceedings under section 15-3-1201 , Idaho Code, or section 15-3-1205 , Idaho Code.
claims.notes: There are three listed exceptions plus carve-outs (prior domiciliary probate, prior appointment). Always say 'subject to exceptions'. Relevant to a house where the owner died years ago and nobody opened probate — refer to an attorney. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 15-3-1201 lets a successor collect a decedent's debts owed and tangible personal property by affidavit, 30 days after death, if the probate estate's value less liens and encumbrances does not exceed $100,000 and no application or petition for a personal representative or summary administration is pending or granted anywhere.
claims.quotedLanguage: (a) Thirty (30) days after the death of a decedent, any person indebted to the decedent or having possession of tangible personal property or an instrument evidencing a debt, obligation, stock or chose in action belonging to the decedent shall make payment of the indebtedness or deliver the tangible personal property or an instrument evidencing a debt, obligation, stock or chose in action to a person or entity claiming to be the successor of the decedent upon being presented an affidavit made by or on behalf of the successor stating that: (1) The fair market value of the entire estate of the decedent which is subject to probate, wherever located, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000); (2) Thirty (30) days have elapsed since the death of the decedent; (3) No application or petition for the appointment of a personal representative or for summary administration is pending or has been granted in any jurisdiction;
claims.notes: ⚠️ The section's text addresses debts, tangible personal property and instruments — it does not mention real property, and its Part heading is 'Collection of personal property by affidavit'. Pair with pb-ada-small-estate-affidavit-no-real-estate. Threshold wording: statute 'does not exceed $100,000'; Ada page says 'less than $100,000' — quote the statute for the threshold. Future-dated check: the 2026 session subject index lists one PROBATE bill, S1240 (Ch. 79, effective 01/01/2027), which repeals/replaces chapter 5 (guardianship/conservatorship) and amends 15-1-201; it does not amend this section.

claims.claim: Ada County's Court Assistance Office describes the small estate affidavit as usable where the decedent did not own real estate and had personal property with a net value under $100,000; it lets a successor collect property owed to the decedent, is signed before a notary, and is not filed with the court.
claims.quotedLanguage: When a person dies, an affidavit may be used if he or she did not own real estate and had personal property with a net value of less than $100,000. The affidavit allows a successor to collect any property, money or other items owed to the deceased. The successor would complete the affidavit and sign it in front of a notary. The affidavit is not filed with the court.
claims.notes: County guidance, not statute. 'less than $100,000' differs from the statute's 'does not exceed' — on the page, cite the statute for the number and the county page only for 'did not own real estate' and 'not filed with the court'.

claims.claim: Where a surviving spouse is the sole devisee or heir, the spouse may petition for summary administration; after notice and hearing the court may enter a decree with the effect of a formal decree of distribution, and a spouse who elects this route assumes liability for the estate's debts, with no administration of the estate.
claims.quotedLanguage: (a) Upon the testate or intestate death of a person leaving a surviving spouse as the sole devisee or beneficiary, the surviving spouse (or any person claiming title to any property through or under such surviving spouse) may file a verified petition setting out marriage and the death of a person leaving a surviving spouse as the sole devisee or heir. ... This decree shall thereafter have the same effect as a formal decree approving or determining distribution. ... (c) In the event that the surviving spouse (or person claiming through or under the surviving spouse) shall elect to proceed under this section, the surviving spouse shall assume and be liable for any and all indebtedness that might be a claim against the estate of the decedent and there will be no administration of the estate of the decedent.
claims.notes: No dollar threshold in the text. The debt-assumption consequence must always be stated with it. claims.claim: When an Idaho personal representative distributes property in kind, they execute an instrument or deed of distribution as evidence of the distributee's title.
claims.quotedLanguage: If distribution in kind is made, the personal representative shall execute an instrument or deed of distribution assigning, transferring or releasing the assets to the distributee as evidence of the distributee's title to the property.
claims.notes: Pairs with pb-purchaser-from-distributee-protected and the existing ada-recorder-maintains-ownership-documents. claims.claim: A purchaser for value from a distributee who received a deed of distribution from the personal representative takes title free of the rights of interested persons in the estate, whether or not the distribution was proper, and need not inquire whether the representative acted properly.
claims.quotedLanguage: If property distributed in kind or a security interest therein is acquired for value by a purchaser from, or lender to, a distributee who has received an instrument or deed of distribution from the personal representative, or is so acquired by a purchaser from or lender to a transferee from such distributee, the purchaser or lender takes title free of rights of any interested person in the estate and incurs no personal liability to the estate, or to any interested person, whether or not the distribution was proper or supported by court order
claims.notes: Protects the purchaser; says nothing about the distributee's liability to other heirs or creditors (see 15-3-104 / 15-3-1004, not claimed). Do not present distribution-then-sale as a way around creditors. claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 55-601, a conveyance of an estate in real property may be made by a written instrument subscribed by the party disposing of the property or by that party's agent authorised in writing, and the grantee's name and complete mailing address must appear on the instrument. The sale price is not among the elements the section requires.
claims.quotedLanguage: A conveyance of an estate in real property may be made by an instrument in writing, subscribed by the party disposing of the same, or by his agent thereunto authorized by writing. The name of the grantee and his complete mailing address must appear on such instrument.
claims.notes: Mirrors commercial-registry claim idaho-deed-content-requirement-omits-price (source idaho-code-55-601, cached at the uppercase Title55/T55CH6 URL). That claim lives in the separate commercial registry, which residential guides do not resolve, so it is restated here against the lowercase section URL. ⚠️ The statute is SILENT on price — never write that Idaho deeds 'do not state' or 'may not state' a price. Some deeds recite consideration. 'May be made' — the section does not say this is the only way title can pass (wills, court decrees etc. exist); do not write 'must'.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 55-612 provides that using the word 'grant' in a conveyance of a fee simple implies two covenants by the grantor, and no others, unless the conveyance expressly restrains them: that the grantor has not previously conveyed the same estate or any interest in it to anyone else, and that the estate is free from encumbrances done, made or suffered by the grantor or anyone claiming under the grantor.
claims.quotedLanguage: From the use of the word "grant" in any conveyance by which an estate of inheritance, possessory right, or fee simple is to be passed, the following covenants, and none other, on the part of the grantor, for himself and his heirs, to the grantee, his heirs and assigns, are implied, unless restrained by express terms contained in such conveyance: 1. That previous to the time of the execution of such conveyance, the grantor has not conveyed the same estate, or any right, title or interest therein, to any person other than the grantee. 2. That such estate is at the time of the execution of such conveyance free from encumbrances done, made or suffered by the grantor, or any person claiming under him.
claims.notes: Describes what the word 'grant' implies by statute. Do NOT characterise warranty deeds vs quitclaim deeds from this — the statute says nothing about deed names, and the warranties in a 'warranty deed' come from its express terms, which no source here covers. Covenant (2) is limited to encumbrances made or suffered by THIS grantor, not all encumbrances ever.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 55-613 defines 'encumbrances' to include taxes, assessments and all liens upon real property.
claims.quotedLanguage: The term "encumbrances" includes taxes, assessments, and all liens upon real property.
claims.notes: Definition sits in chapter 6 next to 55-612; pair them. Do not use this to say how taxes are prorated at closing — no source here addresses proration.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 55-805, before an instrument may be recorded — unless otherwise expressly provided — its execution must be acknowledged by the person executing it (or by a listed officer, partner, manager or member for an entity), or the execution must be proved, with the acknowledgment or proof certified substantially as prescribed by Idaho's notarial law in chapter 1, title 51. An acknowledgment taken in another state or country according to its laws is also entitled to record.
claims.quotedLanguage: Before an instrument may be recorded, unless it is otherwise expressly provided, its execution must be acknowledged by the person executing it ... or the execution must be proved and the acknowledgment or proof, certified in substantially the manner prescribed by chapter 1, title 51, Idaho Code; provided, that if such instrument shall have been executed and acknowledged in any other state or territory of the United States, or in any foreign country, according to the laws of the state, territory or country wherein such acknowledgment was taken, the same shall be entitled to record
claims.notes: ⚠️ Acknowledgment is a condition of RECORDING, not stated here as a condition of the deed's validity between the parties (see 55-815: unrecorded instruments are valid between the parties). Never write 'a deed is invalid unless notarised'. Title 55 chapter 7 (Acknowledgments) is REPEALED — the old acknowledgment rules moved to the Revised Uniform Law on Notarial Acts, Title 51 chapter 1 (2017). Do not cite 55-701 et seq.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 51-105(1), a notary public taking an acknowledgment must determine, from personal knowledge or satisfactory evidence of identity, that the person appearing and acknowledging has the identity claimed and that the signature on the record is that person's signature.
claims.quotedLanguage: A notary public who takes an acknowledgment of a record shall determine, from personal knowledge or satisfactory evidence of the identity of the individual, that the individual appearing before the notary public and making the acknowledgment has the identity claimed and that the signature on the record is the signature of the individual.
claims.notes: Do not list acceptable ID documents from this section — they are in 51-107, which this claim does not cite.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 51-106 requires a person whose signature or statement is the subject of a notarial act to appear personally before the notary public.
claims.quotedLanguage: If a notarial act relates to a statement made in or a signature executed on a record, the individual making the statement or executing the signature shall appear personally before the notary public.
claims.notes: Must be read with 51-114A: personal appearance can be satisfied by communication technology. Never state 51-106 alone as 'you must be in the room'.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 51-114A allows a remotely located individual to satisfy the personal-appearance requirement of 51-106 by appearing before a notary public through communication technology, which the section defines as a device or process allowing the notary and the individual to communicate simultaneously by sight and sound; the Idaho notary must also meet identity, record-confirmation and audio-visual recording conditions.
claims.quotedLanguage: A remotely located individual may comply with the provisions of section 51-106, Idaho Code, by appearing before a notary public by means of communication technology. ... Allows a notary public and a remotely located individual to communicate with each other simultaneously by sight and sound ... The notary public, or a person acting on behalf of the notary public, creates an audio-visual recording of the performance of the notarial act
claims.notes: The statute PERMITS remote notarisation; it does not oblige any title company, lender or recorder to offer or accept it in a given transaction. Never write 'you can sign remotely'. Write 'Idaho law allows' and that whether a particular closing offers it is up to the closing agent. Extra conditions apply when the signer is outside the United States (51-114A(3)(d)).

claims.claim: Idaho Code 55-808 requires instruments entitled to be recorded to be recorded by the county recorder of the county in which the affected real property is situated.
claims.quotedLanguage: Instruments entitled to be recorded must be recorded by the county recorder of the county in which the real property affected thereby is situated.
claims.notes: For an Ada County property that is the Ada County Recorder regardless of city — recording is county-level, not city-level.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 55-809, an instrument is deemed recorded when, being duly acknowledged or proved and certified, it is deposited in the recorder's office with the proper officer for record.
claims.quotedLanguage: An instrument is deemed to be recorded when, being duly acknowledged, or proved and certified, it is deposited in the recorder's office with the proper officer for record.
claims.notes: Does not address e-recording mechanics; do not extend.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 55-811, every conveyance of real property that is acknowledged or proved, certified and recorded as prescribed by law is, from the time it is filed with the recorder for record, constructive notice of its contents to subsequent purchasers and mortgagees.
claims.quotedLanguage: Every conveyance of real property acknowledged or proved, and certified, and recorded as prescribed by law, from the time it is filed with the recorder for record, is constructive notice of the contents thereof to subsequent purchasers and mortgag(e)es.
claims.notes: The odd 'mortgag(e)es' is the compiler's text on the Legislature page; keep it verbatim in the quote. 'Constructive notice' is a legal term — describe it as the statute's phrase, do not paraphrase into 'everyone is deemed to know'.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 55-606 makes every grant or conveyance of real property conclusive against the grantor and everyone later claiming under the grantor, except a purchaser or encumbrancer who, in good faith and for valuable consideration, acquires a title or lien by an instrument or valid judgment lien that is first duly recorded.
claims.quotedLanguage: Every grant or conveyance of an estate in real property is conclusive against the grantor, also against every one subsequently claiming under him, except a purchaser or encumbrancer, who in good faith, and for a valuable consideration, acquires a title or lien by an instrument or valid judgment lien that is first duly recorded.
claims.notes: Pair with id-recording-act-lease-one-year-carveout (55-812). Describe the mechanism only; whether a given buyer is 'in good faith' is a fact question for counsel.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 55-815 states that an unrecorded instrument is valid as between the parties to it and those who have notice of it.
claims.quotedLanguage: An unrecorded instrument is valid as between the parties thereto and those who have notice thereof.
claims.notes: Use it to explain what recording is FOR (protection against third parties), never to suggest recording is optional or unimportant.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 31-2419 requires all books of record, maps, charts, surveys and other papers on file in a county recorder's office to be open during office hours for inspection by any person, without charge.
claims.quotedLanguage: All books of record, maps, charts, surveys and other papers on file in the recorder's office, must, during office hours, be open for the inspection of any person who may desire to inspect them, and may be inspected without charge
claims.notes: Mirrors commercial claim idaho-recorded-documents-are-public (uppercase URL). Closes the gap noted on ada-recorder-maintains-ownership-documents ('31-2419 not yet read at the Legislature') — it has now been read. ⚠️ Inspection 'without charge' is in-office inspection; COPIES carry fees (Ada fee schedule). Pair with cl-ada-deeds-blocked-online: Ada currently blocks online viewing of deeds, so 'open' does not mean 'downloadable online'.

claims.claim: The Ada County Recorder's Office states that certain document types, including deeds, are currently blocked from viewing or downloading online, and that copies must be requested from the office directly.
claims.quotedLanguage: The following documents are currently blocked from viewing or downloading online. If you need copies, please contact our office directly at ... Affidavits in Lieu of Probate Agreements Deeds Appointment of Successor Trustee
claims.notes: ⚠️ FAST-CHANGING: 'currently' is the county's word; the block could be lifted any time. Cache is from 2026-09-09; I re-fetched the live page on 2026-11-12 to a scratch file (not the cache) and the block list still includes Deeds. The second fragment is the rendered list (Affidavits in Lieu of Probate / Agreements / Deeds / Appointment of Successor Trustee) collapsed to one line. Always present with 31-2419: the record is public and inspectable; the online view of deeds is what is restricted.

claims.claim: Ada County's recording fee schedule places any deed transferring or affecting ownership of a property — including warranty, quitclaim, trustee, probate and tax deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure — in a predictable-fee category of $15.00, which covers the first 30 pages, with an additional $3.00 per page beyond 30.
claims.quotedLanguage: Any deed document transferring or affecting ownership of a property will fall into this category ... Deed in lieu of foreclosure, Deed in Satisfaction of mortgage debt, etc.) $15.00 ... Predictable fees cover the first 30 pages of a document. Documents that exceed 30 pages will be charged an additional $3.00 per page.
claims.notes: ⚠️ FAST-CHANGING fee. This is the county RECORDING fee for the deed document only — never present it as 'closing costs' or as what a seller pays; who pays recording fees is a contract matter no source here addresses. The page also says a document that does not support a recording label needs a cover sheet, which 'may increase the recording fee'. Live page re-checked 2026-11-12 (scratch copy): $15.00 unchanged.

claims.claim: An Idaho county assessor describes Idaho as a non-disclosure state and says that, as a result, the assessor's office depends heavily on the public to provide sales information when property is bought and sold.
claims.quotedLanguage: Since Idaho is a non-disclosure state, the Assessor's office depends heavily on the public to provide sales information when property is bought and sold.
claims.notes: Mirrors commercial claim idaho-is-a-non-disclosure-state. ⚠️ THE SOURCE IS CANYON COUNTY, NOT ADA. It is cited for a statewide characterisation of Idaho law, which is what it asserts. Attribute it ('Canyon County's assessor puts it this way') — never write 'Ada County says'. Ada's own assessor pages do not use the phrase (per commercial-registry notes). ALWAYS publish with cl-recorder-records-open-without-charge and cl-deed-writing-subscribed-grantee-address: the record is open; the price simply is not a required element of the deed. Never write 'Idaho keeps sale prices secret'. Live page re-checked 2026-11-12: sentence still present. NEVER cite 'Idaho Code 63-307A' — it does not exist (see commercial claim idaho-63-307a-does-not-exist).

claims.claim: Idaho's title insurance chapter (Title 41, chapter 27) applies to title insurers, title insurance agents and everyone engaged in the business of title insurance, and that business is defined to include a title insurer's or agent's handling of escrows, settlements or closings incident to a title insurance contract or policy.
claims.quotedLanguage: The provisions of chapter 27, title 41, Idaho Code, shall apply to all title insurance companies, title insurance rating organizations, title insurance agents, applicants for title insurance, policyholders and to all persons and business entities engaged in the business of title insurance. ... The performance of any act included herein by a title insurer or a title insurance agent including, but not limited to, handling of escrows, settlements or closing incident to any contract or policy of title insurance
claims.notes: This is the statutory basis for saying a title company's closing/escrow work falls under the title insurance chapter supervised by the Director of the Department of Insurance. No Department of Insurance consumer web page was cached; the regulator link rests on statute text (41-2707, 41-2711 name the director).

claims.claim: Idaho's Escrow Act (Title 30, chapter 9) does not apply to, among others, Idaho-licensed attorneys performing professional duties (unless running a separate escrow business), banks and credit unions, title insurance companies with a valid certificate of authority and title insurance agents licensed by the Idaho Department of Insurance, and real estate licensees acting incidentally to sales they handle.
claims.quotedLanguage: The requirements of this chapter do not apply to: (1) Any person licensed to practice law in this state while engaged in the performance of his professional duties, except an attorney or law firm actively engaging in a separate business as an escrow agency; ... (3) Title insurance companies having a valid certificate of authority, and title insurance agents having a valid license as a title insurance agent, issued by the Idaho department of insurance; (4) Any real estate company, broker or salesperson licensed by and subject to the jurisdiction of the Idaho real estate commission, while performing acts in the course of or incidental to sales or purchases of real or personal property handled or negotiated by such real estate company, broker or salesperson;
claims.notes: Banks/credit unions are subsection (2), omitted from the quote by ellipsis — the claim text mentions them; if the page cites banks, quote (2) too. Who licenses NON-exempt escrow agencies is not stated in 30-905 (the Department of Finance PDF found in search was an 'unofficial copy' and was not cached) — do not name the Department of Finance as the escrow regulator on the page.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 41-2708(1) bars issuing title insurance on Idaho real property until the title insurer or its agent owns or leases tract indexes and abstract records of the county where the property is located and has caused a search and examination of the title and a determination of insurability to be made in accordance with sound title underwriting practices.
claims.quotedLanguage: No title insurance on real property in the state of Idaho shall be issued unless and until the title insurer or its agent: (a) Owns or leases, separately or jointly with another, tract indexes and abstract records of the county in which the property is located; and (b) Has caused to be made a search and examination of the title and a determination of insurability of title in accordance with sound title underwriting practices.
claims.notes: Do not say a title search 'finds every problem' — the statute requires a search and determination of insurability, not a guarantee of clean title.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 41-2708(3) prohibits a title insurance company or title insurance agent from quoting or charging anyone less than the rate currently filed for the risk with the Department of Insurance, and every title insurer must file its rate schedule with the Director of the Department of Insurance under 41-2707.
claims.quotedLanguage: No title insurance company or title insurance agent shall quote or make any charge for title insurance to any person less than the currently filed rate for such risk with the department of insurance. ... every title insurer or rating organization shall file with the director of the department of insurance its schedule of rates
claims.notes: amendmentHistory is 41-2708's. 41-2707's history note, verbatim: [I.C., sec. 41-2707, as added by 1973, ch. 135, sec. 4, p. 252; am. 1977, ch. 142, sec. 9, p. 310.] 41-2708(3) carves out one narrow exception: a reimbursement or discount of the premium and escrow fees 'in a transaction handled by such title insurance company or title insurance agent involving a bona fide employee's residence'. It also makes anyone giving or receiving an illegal rebate or reduced rate liable for three times the amount. Do not generalise either point beyond that. No actual rate numbers are sourced — never print a title premium.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 41-2711 defines an escrow officer as an officer or employee of a title insurance agent whose duties include handling escrows, settlements, closings and related funds, requires each title insurance agent to file escrow officers' names with the Director of Insurance, and requires a corporate surety bond of at least $10,000 per county, increasing by $10,000 per additional escrow officer in the county, up to a maximum of $50,000.
claims.quotedLanguage: An escrow officer is an officer or an employee of a title insurance agent whose duties include any of the following: handling escrows, settlements, closings, and funds related thereto ... The bond shall be in the minimum amount of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) per county in which the title insurance agent is licensed and increased in increments of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) corresponding to each additional person employed as an escrow officer in the county, provided that the maximum bond required of any title insurance agent shall be fifty thousand dollars ($50,000)
claims.notes: ⚠️ The $50,000 cap is per AGENT, irrespective of counties or officers — not per transaction. Never imply the bond covers a seller's sale proceeds in full. The page should describe the bond as a regulatory requirement, not as consumer protection with a stated payout.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 41-2714, a title insurer may issue closing or settlement protection to a buyer, borrower or lender in a transaction in which a title policy will be issued, limited to loss from a licensed title agent's theft or misappropriation of closing funds or failure to follow agreed written closing instructions; the rate may not exceed $25.00, and no party is required to obtain it.
claims.quotedLanguage: A title insurer may issue closing or settlement protection to a buyer, borrower or lender that is a party to a transaction in which a title insurance policy will be issued. ... Theft or misappropriation of closing or settlement funds in connection with a transaction in which a title insurance policy or title insurance policies will be issued by or on behalf of the title insurer issuing the closing or settlement protection. ... Not exceed twenty-five dollars ($25.00). ... Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a buyer, borrower or lender to obtain closing or settlement protection.
claims.notes: 🚨 TRAP: the statute lists BUYER, BORROWER OR LENDER — the SELLER is not named. Never tell a seller they can buy closing protection. The page states the list as written and lets the omission speak.

claims.claim: IRS instructions direct that Form 1099-S, Proceeds From Real Estate Transactions, be filed to report the sale or exchange of real estate, and that the person responsible for closing the transaction files it — where a Closing Disclosure or other settlement statement lists a settlement agent, that is the person listed as settlement agent.
claims.quotedLanguage: File Form 1099-S, Proceeds From Real Estate Transactions, to report the sale or exchange of real estate. ... If you are the person responsible for closing the transaction, you must file Form 1099-S. If a Closing Disclosure or other settlement form is used, as prescribed under the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (Dodd-Frank), and a person is listed as the settlement agent on the Closing Disclosure or other settlement statement, the person responsible for closing the transaction is the person listed as the settlement agent on that Closing Disclosure or other settlement statement.
claims.notes: Instructions page header reads 'Instructions for Form 1099-S (12/2026)' / 'Revised: 12/2026' — a continuous-use revision for 2026 information filed in early 2027. The instructions also allow a written designation agreement naming a different filer. Not tax advice; the page must not tell a seller whether their sale is reportable.

claims.claim: IRS instructions provide that a Form 1099-S filer need not report the sale of a residence for $250,000 or less ($500,000 if the certification includes an assurance that the seller is married) if the filer receives an acceptable written certification, signed by each seller under penalties of perjury, that the home is the seller's principal residence and the full gain is excludable under section 121; without the certification, the form must be filed.
claims.quotedLanguage: Sale or exchange of a residence (including stock in a cooperative housing corporation) for $250,000 or less if you received an acceptable written assurance (certification) from the seller that such residence is the principal residence (within the meaning of section 121) of the seller and the full amount of the gain on such sale is excludable from gross income under section 121. If the certification includes an assurance that the seller is married, the preceding sentence shall be applied by substituting "$500,000" for "$250,000." ... The certification must be signed by each seller under penalties of perjury. ... You are not required to obtain the certification. However, if you do not obtain it, you must file and furnish Form 1099-S.
claims.notes: ⚠️ This is an exception to REPORTING, not to TAX. Never conflate the two or imply a seller owes or does not owe tax. The certification must also assure no nonqualified use after 2008 — mention or omit, but never shorten the conditions to 'under $250,000 is not reported'. The raw page uses curly quotes around $500,000/$250,000; verify-quotes normalises them.

claims.claim: IRS instructions require the Form 1099-S filer to request the seller's taxpayer identification number no later than the time of closing, and the seller is required to furnish a complete, non-truncated TIN and certify that it is correct.
claims.quotedLanguage: You must request the transferor's TIN no later than the time of closing. ... The transferor is required to furnish their complete, non-truncated TIN and to certify that the TIN is correct.
claims.notes: Explains why the closing agent asks for a Social Security number / W-9. Pairs with ada-recorder-pii-redaction-is-submitter-duty only by contrast (the TIN goes on a tax form, not on the recorded deed) — do not assert where the TIN is or is not written beyond what the sources say.

claims.claim: Under FIRPTA, as the IRS describes it, a disposition of a U.S. real property interest by a foreign person is subject to income tax withholding; buyers, certain purchasers' agents and settlement officers are required to withhold 15% of the amount realized (10% for dispositions before Feb. 17, 2016), and in most cases the buyer is the withholding agent and may be held liable if it fails to withhold.
claims.quotedLanguage: The disposition of a U.S. real property interest by a foreign person (the transferor) is subject to the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act of 1980 (FIRPTA) income tax withholding. ... Persons purchasing U.S. real property interests (transferees) from foreign persons, certain purchasers' agents, and settlement officers are required to withhold 15% (10% for dispositions before Feb. 17, 2016) of the amount realized on the disposition (special rules for foreign corporations). In most cases, the buyer (transferee) is the withholding agent. The transferee must find out if the transferor is a foreign person. If the transferor is a foreign person and the transferee fails to withhold, the transferee may be held liable for the tax.
claims.notes: IRS page last reviewed 21-Jul-2026. '15% generally' — the page lists exceptions and reduced rates (e.g. buyer-residence rules between $300,000 and $1 million). Do not state reduced rates on the page unless separately claimed; say 'generally' and point to the IRS and a tax professional. Never tell a reader whether they are a 'foreign person'.

claims.claim: The IRS lists as an exception from FIRPTA withholding a seller's certification, under penalties of perjury, that the seller is not a foreign person, containing the seller's name, U.S. taxpayer identification number and home address; the certification may be given to a qualified substitute such as the person or title company responsible for closing, and it is not effective if the buyer or substitute knows it is false.
claims.quotedLanguage: The seller (transferor) gives the transferee a certification stating, under penalties of perjury, that the transferor is not a foreign person. The certification should contain the transferor's name, U.S. taxpayer identification number, and home address (or office address, in the case of an entity). The transferor can give the certification to a qualified substitute. ... a qualified substitute is (a) the person (including any attorney or title company) responsible for closing the transaction, other than the transferor's agent, and (b) the transferee's agent. ... The certifications in items 3 and 4 above are not effective if the transferee (or the qualified substitute) has actual knowledge or receives a notice from an agent (or substitute), that the certifications are false.
claims.notes: IRS page last reviewed 15-Jul-2026. This is why a U.S. seller is commonly asked to sign a non-foreign certification at closing — but 'commonly' is NOT sourced; write only what the IRS lists.

claims.claim: Idaho DEQ's septic rules (IDAPA 58.01.03) are administered by Idaho's seven public health districts under a memorandum of understanding with DEQ; the districts conduct site evaluations, issue septic permits, inspect installations and help with property-specific questions, including permit status and existing permit records.
claims.quotedLanguage: Idaho's seven public health districts administer these rules under a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with DEQ. The public health districts conduct site evaluations, issue septic system permits, inspect installations, and assist with property-specific questions about permitting, existing systems, and permit records. ... Permit status and existing permit records
claims.notes: Pairs with existing claim ada-septic-authority-cdh (CDH is the district for Ada County). DEQ writes the rule; the health district is the office a seller actually deals with. DEQ's page says to contact the district 'for the county where the property is located' — do not route an Ada County seller to DEQ for a permit file.

claims.claim: DEQ says a property owner must obtain a public health district permit to have an individual septic system installed, and should have a site evaluation performed by the health district and a licensed installer before purchasing property and applying for a permit.
claims.quotedLanguage: To have a septic system installed, the property owner must obtain a permit from a public health district . The property owner should have a site evaluation performed by the public health district and a licensed septic system installer before purchasing property and applying for a permit.
claims.notes: ⚠️ TRAP: this is about INSTALLING a new system (it is advice to a buyer of unbuilt land), and it is a 'should', not a rule. Never present it as a requirement that an existing system be evaluated at sale.

claims.claim: Under IDAPA 58.01.03, every owner of real property is jointly and individually responsible for storing, treating and disposing of the blackwaste and wastewater generated on that property.
claims.quotedLanguage: Every owner of real property is jointly and individually responsible for: ... Storing, treating, and disposing of blackwaste and wastewater generated on that property.
claims.notes: Rule text from the current adminrules.idaho.gov PDF (section 001.03.a.i; provision dated 3-31-22). Describe only; never tell a reader what this means for their liability after a sale.

claims.claim: Under IDAPA 58.01.03, except for listed exceptions, no one may modify, repair, expand or install an individual or subsurface sewage disposal system in Idaho without a valid installation permit authorizing that work.
claims.quotedLanguage: Except as specified in Subsection 005.02 no person may modify, repair or expand or install any individual or subsurface sewage disposal system within the state of Idaho unless there is a valid installation permit authorizing that activity.
claims.notes: Section 005.01 (7-1-25). There ARE exceptions in 005.02 that this page does not enumerate — always say 'with listed exceptions'.

claims.claim: IDAPA 58.01.03 defines a failing system to include one that fails to accept blackwaste and wastewater or discharges it into waters or onto the ground surface, and requires the owner of a failing system to obtain a permit and repair it as soon as practical after becoming aware of the failure, or as directed with proper notice from the Director.
claims.quotedLanguage: Failing System. Any system that exhibits one (1) or more of the following characteristics: ... Fails to accept blackwaste and wastewater; or ... Discharges blackwaste or wastewater into the waters or onto the ground surface. ... The owner of any failing system must obtain a permit and repair the failing system: ... As soon as practical after the owner becomes aware of its failure; or ... As directed with proper notice from the Director.
claims.notes: Definition 003.15 and duty 004.05. The definition has a third limb (not meeting the intent in 004.01) not quoted here — say 'includes'. ⚠️ Never imply a seller can avoid this duty by selling as-is; and never say whether a particular system is 'failing'.

claims.claim: Under IDAPA 58.01.03 the Director may attach operation, maintenance and monitoring procedures to an installation permit, and those requirements, including effluent sampling, are perpetual unless the system is not installed, is removed, abandoned or replaced, or the permit is amended or revoked.
claims.quotedLanguage: The Director may require, as a condition of issuing a permit, specific operation, maintenance, and monitoring procedures be observed. Those procedures will be contained in the installation permit. ... All operation, maintenance, and monitoring requirements of installation permits including effluent sampling must be perpetual unless: ... The system is removed, abandoned, or replaced; or ... The permit is amended or revoked by the Director.
claims.notes: Section 005.12. Matters at sale because the conditions travel with the permit, not the seller — the reason to read the permit itself. Do not claim any particular system type carries such conditions; the rule says the Director MAY require them.

claims.claim: DEQ's homeowner septic guide (January 2001) says a tank's location can be found from plot plans, septic inspection records, drawings or the house plumbing; recommends that an average family of four have its tank pumped every three to five years; and advises keeping a permanent record of maintenance, repairs, sludge and scum levels, pumping, drainfield condition and backups.
claims.quotedLanguage: The location of your septic tank can be determined from plot plans, septic system inspection records, architectural or landscape drawings, or from observations of the house plumbing. ... It is recommended that an average family of four have its septic tank pumped out every three to five years. ... Maintain a permanent record of any septic system maintenance, repair, sludge and scum levels, pumping, drainfield condition, household backups, and operations notes.
claims.notes: ⚠️ OLD GUIDANCE: dated January 2001, but CDH still links it from its current septic page as the homeowner's guide. MEDIUM confidence for that reason. It is a recommendation, not a rule — always attribute it ('DEQ's guide recommends'). The same booklet elsewhere says 'every three years (or as determined by your inspections)'; if the interval is used, quote the family-of-four sentence and attribute it.

claims.claim: Central District Health takes public records requests through a form on its About page and asks requesters to be specific about the documents they want.
claims.quotedLanguage: To submit a public records request, complete the form above. Be specific regarding the document(s) you are requesting.
claims.jurisdiction: Ada, Boise, Elmore and Valley counties, Idaho
claims.notes: ⚠️ The CDH septic page cached 2026-09-09 (source cdh-septic) carried an online 'Septic System Search' with a note that records date to 1971 and some pre-2000 Ada records are missing. That section is GONE from the live page as of 2026-11-12. Do not cite the search or the 1971 note. This page does not say what a septic file contains or how long a request takes — say neither.

claims.claim: Central District Health describes a mortgage survey as something a lender often requests, to locate a well or septic system and check the water and sewage systems before a property sale, and says it provides water quality testing and mortgage survey inspections of private wells and septic systems.
claims.quotedLanguage: A mortgage survey is often requested by a lender to determine the location of a well or septic system to check water and sewage systems prior to a property sale. ... CDH provides drinking water quality testing and mortgage survey inspections of private wells and septic systems.
claims.jurisdiction: Ada, Boise, Elmore and Valley counties, Idaho
claims.notes: ⚠️ LENDER TRAP: this is CDH saying lenders OFTEN request it. It is not a statement that any lender or loan program requires it, and it is not a legal requirement at sale. Always attribute to CDH and keep the word 'often'.

claims.claim: CDH's mortgage survey fee schedule dated July 2026 lists $178 for a well-only survey plus a $20 lab fee, $178 for septic only, $178 for well and septic plus a $20 lab fee, and $178 plus the lab fee for a revisit.
claims.quotedLanguage: Mortgage Survey Fees: – July 2026 MS – Well Only – $178 (plus lab fee of $20) MS – Septic Only – $178 MS – Well and Septic – $178 (plus lab fee of $20) MS – Lab Fee – $20 MS – Revisit – $178 (plus lab fee of $20)
claims.jurisdiction: Ada, Boise, Elmore and Valley counties, Idaho
claims.notes: FAST-CHANGING: CDH resets fees each July. Always state with 'as of CDH's July 2026 schedule'. Re-check before every refresh.

claims.claim: CDH's mortgage survey information sheet requires a complete, signed application with the legal description and county parcel number, a plot plan showing the septic tank, drainfield and all domestic wells relative to the house, the fees, and a pumping receipt if the tank has been or will be pumped; the inspector must have access to the drainfield, tank and well head, and results are available three to five days after sampling.
claims.quotedLanguage: Application must be filled out thoroughly. Name, addresses, phone number, email, legal description, location, county parcel #, and directions to property. All questions answered and then signed and dated. ... A plot plan must be drawn on the application showing the location of the septic tank, drainfield, and all domestic wells in relationship to the house. ... If the septic tank has been or will be pumped, we will need a copy of the pumping receipt. ... The inspector must have access to the entire area of the drainfield, septic tank, and well head. ... Survey results will be available 3-5 days after the sample is taken.
claims.jurisdiction: Ada, Boise, Elmore and Valley counties, Idaho
claims.notes: Sheet is footer-dated 6/11/25 and still linked from the live CDH page. The 3–5 day figure is CDH's own estimate for results after sampling, not a total turnaround — never present it as 'the survey takes a week'.

claims.claim: CDH says that in Idaho private well owners are responsible for ensuring their water is safe to drink, that private water may have to be tested for house sales if a lender or buyer requires it, and that well water should be tested once a year for bacteria and nitrates.
claims.quotedLanguage: In Idaho, private well owners are responsible for ensuring their water is safe to drink. ... Private water sources can be required to be tested under other regulations or requirements if the water is being used for small daycares, small food processors, bottled water plants, foster/care homes, and house sales if required by lender or buyer. ... You should test your well water once a year for bacteria and nitrates.
claims.jurisdiction: Ada, Boise, Elmore and Valley counties, Idaho
claims.notes: ⚠️ 'if required by lender or buyer' — testing at sale is driven by a lender or buyer, per CDH; it is not stated as a legal requirement of every sale. Do not convert this into 'lenders require a water test'.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 42-238(11) requires every well driller — including for domestic wells excepted under 42-227 — to complete a well driller's report and deposit it with the IDWR director within 30 days after the well is completed; the reports become a permanent record available for public use.
claims.quotedLanguage: every well driller is hereby required to keep available for inspection at the well site a daily well log and pertinent data concerning each well, and its construction or abandonment, that is constructed or abandoned under the driller's direction in Idaho, including wells excepted under sections 42-227 and 42-228 , Idaho Code, and to complete a report on forms furnished by the director. These reports shall be properly prepared and signed by the driller and deposited with the director within thirty (30) days following the completion of the well. ... The reports shall become a permanent record in the office of the director for hydrologic and geologic analysis and research and shall be available for public use.
claims.notes: Chapter index checked 2026-11-12: one 42-238 entry, no future-dated version. The statute does not say a report exists for every well — older wells may predate it; pair with ws-idwr-well-construction-search for coverage.

claims.claim: IDWR's Well Construction Search lets anyone look up wells and view the related well driller's reports; IDWR says the database contains most reports from July 1987 on, that it has assigned a unique well tag number to each well since 1997, printed on a metal plate fixed to the above-ground casing, that the tag number is the first-listed of its search methods, which it lists in order of effectiveness, and that wells can also be searched by township/range/section, physical address, or the name of the owner when the well was drilled.
claims.quotedLanguage: Search for wells in Idaho and view the related Well Driller's Reports (Logs). ... The database contains most of the Well Drillers Reports from July 1987 to current. ... The search methods are listed in the order of effectiveness. Use only ONE of the methods listed: Input the Well Tag Number (for example: D0012345). ... Beginning in 1997, IDWR began assigning a unique well tag number to each well. ... A well's tag number is printed on a metal plate ... that is welded or riveted to the portion of the metal well casing that sits above ground level. ... Input the physical address of the well. ... Input the last name of the person OR the organization who owned the well when it was drilled.
claims.notes: 'most' — IDWR's own hedge. A well drilled before July 1987 may have no report in the database; never say 'every well has a log online'. The plate-size parenthetical is elided with '...' because the cache encodes the inch marks as ″, which the verifier does not decode.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 42-235 requires the driller or well owner to obtain a permit from the IDWR director before beginning construction of any well or changing a well's construction, with a $75 charge for a domestic or monitoring well and $200 otherwise.
claims.quotedLanguage: Prior to beginning construction of any well, or changing the construction of any well, the driller or well owner shall obtain a permit from the director of the department of water resources to protect the public health, safety and welfare and the environment, and to prevent the waste of water or mixture of water from different aquifers. There shall be a seventy-five dollar ($75.00) charge for the permit if the well is to be used for domestic or monitoring purposes. If the well is to be used for other than domestic or monitoring purposes, the charge for the permit shall be two hundred dollars ($200).
claims.notes: A DRILLING permit is not a WATER RIGHT permit. 42-227 exempts domestic wells from the water-right permit (42-229) — not from this drilling permit. Keep the two separate in prose.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 42-227 provides that, except for certain new subdivision diversions in regulated groundwater areas, drilling a well and withdrawing water for domestic purposes as defined in 42-111 is not subject to the water-right permit requirement of 42-229; rights to groundwater for such domestic purposes may be acquired by withdrawal and use, and domestic wells are subject to inspection by IDWR and DEQ.
claims.quotedLanguage: Except as provided in subsection (4) of this section, excavation and opening of wells and the withdrawal of water therefrom for domestic purposes or uses as defined in section 42-111 , Idaho Code, shall not be subject to permit requirements under section 42-229 , Idaho Code. Rights to ground water for such domestic purposes may be acquired by withdrawal and use. (2) Wells and withdrawal devices for domestic purposes or uses shall be subject to inspection by the department of water resources and the department of environmental quality.
claims.notes: ⚠️ FAST-MOVING: amended 2025 and 2026, same as 42-111. Subsection (4) (new subdivision diversions filed on/after July 1, 2025 in moratorium/critical/management areas) is summarised, not quoted — never apply it to a reader's parcel.

claims.claim: IDWR reports that the 2025 Legislature passed Senate Bill 1083a revising the domestic-use, shared-well and subdivision statutes, and that Senate Bill 1222, signed February 17, 2026, further revised them, effective that day, changing the requirements for establishing a domestic water right without an IDWR permit.
claims.quotedLanguage: The 2025 Idaho Legislature passed Senate Bill 1083a revising several statutes dealing with domestic uses of water, shared wells, and subdivisions. On February 17, 2026, Governor Little signed Senate Bill 1222, which further revised the statutes dealing with ground water wells and domestic uses. These statutory changes became effective on February 17, 2026.
claims.notes: Agency description of the change, used only to tell the reader the law moved recently. The statute pages (42-111, 42-227) carry 'am. 2026, ch. 2', consistent with this.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 42-248 requires anyone owning or claiming a water right represented by a court decree, a claim filed with IDWR, or an IDWR permit or license to notify IDWR of any change in ownership of any part of the right, or of the owner's mailing address, within 120 days, using forms acceptable to the director.
claims.quotedLanguage: All persons owning or claiming ownership of a right to use the water of this state, whether the right is represented by decree of the court, by claim to a water right filed with the department of water resources or by permit or license issued by the director of the department, shall provide notice to the department of any change in ownership of any part of the water right or of any change in the owner's mailing address. Notice shall be provided within one hundred twenty (120) days of any change using forms acceptable to the director.
claims.notes: ⚠️ SCOPE TRAP: the duty attaches to rights represented by a decree, filed claim, or permit/license. Whether a particular domestic well has any such record is a parcel fact — never assert that a seller's well does or does not. The statute places the duty on 'all persons owning or claiming ownership' — it does not say 'the buyer' or 'the seller'; do not assign it to either. Chapter index checked: no future-dated version.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 42-248 a notice of change of water right ownership must carry a $25 filing fee per right ($100 per right if the records are to show the right divided), with no fee for a claim pending in an adjudication; it must be accompanied by deeds, court decrees or other evidence of conveyance; and IDWR updating its records is not a determination of who owns the right.
claims.quotedLanguage: A filing fee of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) per right shall accompany a notice of change of water right ownership, provided that the fee shall be one hundred dollars ($100) per right if a request is made to change the department's records to reflect a division in the ownership of the water right. No fee is required for a notice of change of ownership of a claim pending in a water rights adjudication. ... A notice of change of water right ownership of all or part of a water right shall be accompanied by deeds, court decrees, or other evidence of conveyance of the water right and how the water right is divided if the change divides the water right among multiple owners. ... Any action by the department updating the ownership of a water right in the department's records or returning the notice of change of ownership to the person filing the notice is not a determination of water right ownership
claims.notes: Subsections (4), (5), (8). Ownership disputes go to adjudication or quiet title per (8) — point to an attorney, never resolve.

claims.claim: IDWR says a landowner may have acquired a valid water right with the land if water was used on the property before they acquired it, the prior owner did not reserve the right in the deed, and the right has not been forfeited through five or more years of non-use; and it tells buyers of property with a water right or adjudication claim to make sure they are listed as current owner with a correct address.
claims.quotedLanguage: You might have acquired a valid water right along with your land if: water was used on your property before you acquired it, the person you acquired the property from did not "reserve" the water right in the deed conveying the property to you, and the water right has not been forfeited due to five or more years of non-use. ... If you purchase property that has with it a water right or adjudication claim, make certain that you are listed as the current owner and that your address is correct.
claims.notes: IDWR says 'might' — agency guidance, not a rule of title. The deed-reservation point is the one a seller controls; any reservation question is for an attorney.
