claims.notes: Scope trap: 'a sale made by a trustee under this act' means a nonjudicial trustee's sale under a deed of trust (Title 45, chapter 15). Do NOT extend 'no right to redeem' to a judicial mortgage foreclosure or to a county tax deed (see id-tax-deed-redemption-fourteen-months, which is a different process with its own redemption rule). The bar runs to persons 'to whom notice is given' and those claiming through them; never tell a reader whether they were validly given notice.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 45-1508 says a failure to give notice to one person does not affect the validity of the sale as to persons who were notified or who had actual knowledge of the sale, and that a failure to comply with section 45-1506 does not affect the validity of a sale in favor of a purchaser in good faith for value, or that purchaser's successor.
claims.quotedLanguage: The failure to give notice to any of such persons by mailing, personal service, posting or publication in accordance with section 45-1506, Idaho Code, shall not affect the validity of the sale as to persons so notified nor as to any such persons having actual knowledge of the sale. Furthermore, any failure to comply with the provisions of section 45-1506, Idaho Code, shall not affect the validity of a sale in favor of a purchaser in good faith for value at or after such sale, or any successor in interest thereof.
claims.notes: State what the section says and stop. Whether a particular sale can be challenged, and who counts as a purchaser in good faith for value, are court questions. Do not write 'a sale cannot be undone' and do not write 'a defective sale can be undone'.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1506(11), the purchaser at a trustee's sale is entitled to possession of the property on the tenth day following the sale, and anyone who remains in possession after that under any interest except one prior to the deed of trust is deemed a tenant at sufferance.
claims.quotedLanguage: The purchaser at the trustee's sale shall be entitled to possession of the property on the tenth day following the sale, and any persons remaining in possession thereafter under any interest except one prior to the deed of trust shall be deemed to be tenants at sufferance.
claims.notes: 'On the tenth day following the sale' is the statute's wording; do not convert it to 'you have 10 days to move out' or to a calendar date. 'Entitled to possession' is a legal entitlement, not a description of a lockout: the statute does not authorise self-help removal and this claim must not be used to say so. Note the carve-out for an interest 'prior to the deed of trust'. For tenants, must be stated together with the federal PTFA claims (as-ptfa-*).

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1506(9) and (10), the purchaser at the sale pays the price bid forthwith, the trustee then executes and delivers the trustee's deed, and that deed conveys the interest the grantor had or had the power to convey when the trust deed was signed, together with any interest the grantor or the grantor's successors acquired afterwards.
claims.quotedLanguage: The purchaser at the sale shall forthwith pay the price bid and upon receipt of payment the trustee shall execute and deliver the trustee's deed to such purchaser ... The trustee's deed shall convey to the purchaser the interest in the property which the grantor had, or had the power to convey, at the time of the execution by him of the trust deed together with any interest the grantor or his successors in interest acquired after the execution of such trust deed.
claims.notes: 'Grantor' in this chapter is the borrower who signed the deed of trust. Explain that once in prose.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1510(1), once the trustee's deed is recorded in the county where the property is located, the recitals in the deed and in the affidavits required by 45-1506(7) are prima facie evidence of their truth in any court and are conclusive in favor of a purchaser in good faith for value; the deed is deemed effective as of the date and time of the sale if it is recorded within fifteen days after the sale.
claims.quotedLanguage: When the trustee's deed is recorded in the deed records of the county where the property described in the deed is located, the recitals contained in the deed and in the affidavits required under section 45-1506 (7), Idaho Code, shall be prima facie evidence in any court of the truth of the recitals and the affidavits. However, the recitals and affidavits are conclusive in favor of a purchaser in good faith for value or any successor in interest thereof. For purposes of this section, the trustee's deed shall be deemed effective as of the date and time on which the sale was held if such deed is recorded within fifteen (15) days after the date of sale or the first business day following the fifteenth day if the county recorder of the county in which the property is located is closed on the fifteenth day.
claims.notes: The fifteen days is about when the deed is deemed EFFECTIVE, 'for purposes of this section'. It is not a deadline for the former owner and not a redemption window. Do not describe what happens if the deed is recorded later; the section does not say.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 45-1510(2) provides that where a trustee's sale is invalid by reason of the automatic stay provisions of the U.S. bankruptcy code, a stay order issued by a court, or otherwise, recording a notice of rescission of the trustee's deed restores record title and lien priorities to where they stood before the sale, and that only the trustee or beneficiary who caused the deed to be recorded, or a successor, may record that notice.
claims.quotedLanguage: Where a trustee's sale held pursuant to section 45-1506, Idaho Code, is invalid by reason of automatic stay provisions of the U.S. bankruptcy code, or a stay order issued by any court of competent jurisdiction or otherwise, recordation of a notice of rescission of the trustee's deed shall restore the condition of record title to the real property described in the trustee's deed and the existence and priority of all lienholders to the status quo prior to the trustee's sale. Only the trustee or beneficiary who caused the trustee's deed to be recorded, or his/its successor in interest, may record a notice of rescission.
claims.notes: HIGH RISK OF OVER-READING. This is a mechanism for the TRUSTEE OR BENEFICIARY to unwind a sale that was already invalid; the former owner cannot record it. It is NOT a right to get the house back and NOT advice that filing bankruptcy after a sale reverses it. The section says nothing about a bankruptcy filed after the sale. Always attribute, always send the reader to a bankruptcy or real estate attorney.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 45-1507 requires the trustee to apply the proceeds of the trustee's sale in a fixed order: first to the expenses of the sale, including a reasonable trustee's charge and a reasonable attorney's fee; second to the obligation secured by the trust deed; third to persons having recorded liens subsequent to the interest of the trustee in the trust deed, as their interests may appear; and fourth, any surplus to the grantor of the trust deed or the grantor's successor in interest entitled to it.
claims.quotedLanguage: The trustee shall apply the proceeds of the trustee's sale as follows: (1) To the expenses of the sale, including a reasonable charge by the trustee and a reasonable attorney's fee. (2) To the obligation secured by the trust deed. (3) To any persons having recorded liens subsequent to the interest of the trustee in the trust deed as their interests may appear. (4) The surplus, if any, to the grantor of the trust deed or to his successor in interest entitled to such surplus.
claims.notes: Surplus exists only 'if any', after three earlier tiers. Never imply a surplus is likely, never estimate one. The section sets the ORDER; it does not say when the trustee pays, how a grantor claims the money, or what happens when a lien is disputed. Unchanged since 1957. Do not carry this order over to a county tax deed sale.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1512, a money judgment for the balance due on the obligation that the deed of trust secured may be sought at any time within 3 months after a sale under the deed of trust.
claims.quotedLanguage: At any time within 3 months after any sale under a deed of trust, as hereinbefore provided, a money judgment may be sought for the balance due upon the obligation for which such deed of trust was given as security
claims.notes: The statute writes '3 months', not 90 days; do not convert. The window is for SEEKING the judgment (filing the action), not for obtaining it. It covers 'the obligation for which such deed of trust was given as security' and says nothing about a different loan secured by a junior lien that the sale wiped out; do not claim those debts are barred or limited by this section.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 45-1512 requires the court, before entering a deficiency judgment, to find the fair market value of the property at the time of sale; the judgment may not exceed the amount by which the entire indebtedness due at the time of sale exceeds that fair market value, with interest from the date of sale, and in no event may it exceed the difference between the amount the property sold for and the entire indebtedness secured by the deed of trust.
claims.quotedLanguage: Before rendering judgment the court shall find the fair market value of the real property sold at the time of sale. The court may not render judgment for more than the amount by which the entire amount of indebtedness due at the time of sale exceeds the fair market value at that time, with interest from date of sale, but in no event may the judgment exceed the difference between the amount for which such property was sold and the entire amount of the indebtedness secured by the deed of trust.
claims.notes: TWO ceilings and the lower one governs: (debt minus fair market value) and (debt minus sale price). Do not illustrate with invented dollar figures (rule 7). Do not call Idaho a 'non-recourse' or an 'anti-deficiency' state; the section limits a deficiency judgment, it does not abolish it. The court finds fair market value; nobody else's estimate, including ours, stands in for that.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1506(15), on or after the tenth day following the sale, if the purchaser reasonably determines the property is unoccupied, the purchaser may remove nontitled personal property and place it in suitable storage, and may dispose of it only after ninety days' written notice sent by first class mail to the last known address of the last known occupant and posted in a conspicuous place on the premises; an owner who does not claim the property within those ninety days loses all rights in it.
claims.quotedLanguage: On or after the tenth day, as provided in subsection (11) of this section, if the property is reasonably determined by the purchaser to be unoccupied, the purchaser may: ... Remove any nontitled personal property from the premises and place it in suitable storage. The purchaser may dispose of the nontitled personal property only after providing ninety (90) days' written notice as follows: (i) First class mail to the last known address of the last known occupant of the property; and (ii) Posting a notice in a conspicuous place on the premises ... If the owner of the nontitled personal property fails to claim the nontitled personal property within ninety (90) days of the date that written notice was provided under paragraph (b) of this subsection, then any and all of his rights in said property shall extinguish
claims.notes: Applies ONLY where the property is 'reasonably determined by the purchaser to be unoccupied'. It is not a rule about belongings in an occupied house. Titled personal property (paragraph (a)) is handled 'in the manner described by applicable law', which this claim does not cover. Do not confuse this ninety days with the federal 90-day tenant notice.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 6-310 lets an action exclusively for possession of a tract of five acres or less be brought where the occupant is a tenant at sufferance under 45-1506(11); the complaint may state that no notice is required for that reason, the court must schedule a trial within twelve days from the filing of the complaint, and the summons, complaint and notice of trial setting must be served not less than five days before the trial date.
claims.quotedLanguage: In an action exclusively for possession of a tract of land of five (5) acres or less for the nonpayment of rent ... or in the event the tenant is a tenant at sufferance pursuant to section 45-1506 (11), Idaho Code, it is sufficient to state in the complaint: ... That all notices required by law have been served upon the defendant in the required manner or no notice is required because the defendant is a tenant at sufferance pursuant to section 45-1506 (11), Idaho Code ... at the time of issuance of the summons, the court shall schedule a trial within twelve (12) days from the filing of the complaint, and the service of the summons, complaint and notice of trial setting on the defendant shall be not less than five (5) days before the day of trial appointed by the court.
claims.notes: This is what the purchaser's court route looks like; it is a COURT process, which is the point to make. Limited by its terms to 'a tract of land of five (5) acres or less'; larger tracts are not covered by this claim. The twelve days is a scheduling rule for the court, not a move-out deadline and not a prediction of how long a case takes. Only subsections (1) and (2) are relied on. Sections on judgment, writ and removal (6-311 onward) were NOT read; say nothing about what happens after the trial. 'No notice is required' is Idaho's pleading rule and must not be presented as overriding the federal tenant notice (as-ptfa-90-day-notice).

claims.claim: The federal Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act provides that, in a foreclosure on a federally-related mortgage loan or on any dwelling or residential real property, the immediate successor in interest takes the property subject to giving any bona fide tenant a notice to vacate at least 90 days before the effective date of the notice; a tenant without a lease, or with a lease terminable at will under state law, is covered by that same 90 day notice.
claims.quotedLanguage: In the case of any foreclosure on a federally-related mortgage loan or on any dwelling or residential real property after the date of enactment of this title [May 20, 2009], any immediate successor in interest in such property pursuant to the foreclosure shall assume such interest subject to ... the provision, by such successor in interest of a notice to vacate to any bona fide tenant at least 90 days before the effective date of such notice ... without a lease or with a lease terminable at will under State law, subject to the receipt by the tenant of the 90 day notice under subsection (1), except that nothing under this section shall affect the requirements for termination of any Federal- or State-subsidized tenancy or of any State or local law that provides longer time periods or other additional protections for tenants.
claims.notes: Quoted from the statutory note printed under 12 U.S.C. 5220 in the U.S. Code, 2024 Edition (section 702 of Pub. L. 111-22 as amended). Protects BONA FIDE TENANTS only; the former owner is not one (see as-ptfa-bona-fide-definition and as-ptfa-does-not-cover-homeowners). Idaho 45-1506(11) calls post-sale occupants tenants at sufferance and 6-310 says no notice is required; this page must state both and must NOT resolve how they interact for a given tenancy. That is an attorney question.

claims.claim: Under the Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act, a bona fide tenant under a bona fide lease entered into before the notice of foreclosure may occupy the premises until the end of the remaining lease term, except that the successor in interest may terminate the lease effective on the date of sale of the unit to a purchaser who will occupy it as a primary residence, subject to the 90 day notice. For this purpose the date of a notice of foreclosure is deemed to be the date complete title is transferred to the successor as a result of a court order or under provisions in a mortgage, deed of trust or security deed.
claims.quotedLanguage: under any bona fide lease entered into before the notice of foreclosure to occupy the premises until the end of the remaining term of the lease, except that a successor in interest may terminate a lease effective on the date of sale of the unit to a purchaser who will occupy the unit as a primary residence, subject to the receipt by the tenant of the 90 day notice under paragraph (1) ... the date of a notice of foreclosure shall be deemed to be the date on which complete title to a property is transferred to a successor entity or person as a result of an order of a court or pursuant to provisions in a mortgage, deed of trust, or security deed.
claims.notes: The 'notice of foreclosure' definition is counter-intuitive: it is the date title transfers, not the date a notice of default or notice of sale was recorded. Quote it rather than paraphrase. Do not tell a tenant or a landlord whether a particular lease qualifies.

claims.claim: The Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act treats a lease or tenancy as bona fide only if the tenant is not the mortgagor or the mortgagor's child, spouse or parent, the lease or tenancy was the result of an arms-length transaction, and the rent is not substantially less than fair market rent or is reduced or subsidized due to a federal, state or local subsidy.
claims.quotedLanguage: a lease or tenancy shall be considered bona fide only if ... the mortgagor or the child, spouse, or parent of the mortgagor under the contract is not the tenant ... the lease or tenancy was the result of an arms-length transaction ... the lease or tenancy requires the receipt of rent that is not substantially less than fair market rent for the property or the unit's rent is reduced or subsidized due to a Federal, State, or local subsidy.
claims.notes: All three conditions are cumulative ('only if ... and'). A family member of the borrower renting the house is outside the definition by its terms. Never tell a reader their tenancy is or is not bona fide.

claims.claim: The Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act expired at the end of 2014 and was restored by section 304 of Public Law 115-174. The Federal Reserve Board's letter CA 18-4 states that the restored law became effective on June 23, 2018, that the restored act does not include an expiration date, and that the law is self-executing, with no federal agency having authority to issue regulations implementing it or to interpret it. The U.S. Code, 2024 Edition, prints the tenant-protection section as restored and revived.
claims.quotedLanguage: which became effective on June 23, 2018. The law protects tenants from immediate eviction by persons or entities that become owners of residential property through the foreclosure process ... The law is self-executing; no federal agency has authority to issue regulations implementing the law or to interpret the law. ... which expired on December 31, 2014. Section 704 contained the Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act of 2009's sunset provisions; the restored act does not include an expiration date. ... provisions of law amended by such section, and any regulations promulgated pursuant to such section, as in effect on Dec. 30, 2014, restored and revived
claims.notes: This is the 'is it still in force' claim. Evidence of currency: a 2018 Federal Reserve supervisory letter (page last updated June 22, 2018) plus the 2024 Edition of the U.S. Code on govinfo.gov, which still prints the section with the restoration note. Neither is a statement dated 2026. Re-check the next U.S. Code edition before each refresh. 'Self-executing ... no agency may interpret' is why there is no regulation to cite.

claims.claim: The Federal Reserve Board's letter CA 18-4 states that the Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act does not cover tenants facing eviction in a non-foreclosed property, tenants with a fraudulent lease, tenants who enter into lease agreements after a foreclosure sale, or homeowners in foreclosure, and that the law does not affect any state or local law that provides longer time periods or other additional protections for tenants.
claims.quotedLanguage: The law does not cover tenants facing eviction in a non-foreclosed property, tenants with a fraudulent lease, tenants who enter in lease agreements after a foreclosure sale, or homeowners in foreclosure. Additionally, the law does not affect the requirements of any State or local law that provides for longer time periods or extends additional protections to tenants.
claims.notes: Attribute to the Federal Reserve letter, which is the agency's description of the law, not the statute text. The statute reaches the same result for owners through the bona fide definition (the mortgagor cannot be the tenant). This is the sentence that tells a former OWNER the 90 days is not theirs.

claims.claim: The Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681c(a), bars a consumer reporting agency from making a consumer report that contains any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes, that antedates the report by more than seven years; civil suits and civil judgments may be reported for seven years from the date of entry or until the governing statute of limitations has expired, whichever is longer.
claims.quotedLanguage: no consumer reporting agency may make any consumer report containing any of the following items of information: ... Civil suits, civil judgments, and records of arrest that, from date of entry, antedate the re port by more than seven years or until the governing statute of limitations has expired, whichever is the longer period. ... Any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes which antedates the report by more than seven years.
claims.notes: THE STATUTE DOES NOT USE THE WORD 'FORECLOSURE'. A foreclosure falls, if anywhere, under the catch-all in paragraph (5), and the page must say the statute does not name it rather than assert 'a foreclosure stays seven years' as a quoted rule. The statute does not say from what event the seven years is counted for a foreclosure; do not state a start date. 're port' is a typesetting break in the govinfo HTML and is reproduced so the quote verifies; never render it in prose. Must be stated with as-fcra-exceptions-large-transactions. This is a limit on REPORTING, not on credit scores or on any lender's underwriting waiting period.

claims.claim: Under 15 U.S.C. 1681c(b), the seven-year and ten-year reporting limits in subsection (a)(1) through (5) do not apply to a consumer credit report used in connection with a credit transaction involving a principal amount of $150,000 or more, the underwriting of life insurance with a face amount of $150,000 or more, or the employment of an individual at an annual salary of $75,000 or more.
claims.quotedLanguage: The provisions of paragraphs (1) through (5) of subsection (a) are not applicable in the case of any consumer credit report to be used in connection with ... a credit transaction involving, or which may reasonably be expected to involve, a principal amount of $150,000 or more; ... the underwriting of life insurance involving, or which may reasonably be expected to involve, a face amount of $150,000 or more; or ... the employment of any individual at an annual salary which equals, or which may reasonably be expected to equal $75,000, or more.
claims.notes: Directly relevant to a later mortgage application, which will often involve a principal amount at or above the threshold. Say what the exception is; do not say what any credit bureau or lender actually does in practice (not sourced).

claims.claim: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau states that a credit reporting company generally can report most negative information for seven years, that information about a lawsuit or a judgment can be reported for seven years or until the statute of limitations runs out, whichever is longer, and that no one has the right to remove accurate negative information from a credit report.
claims.quotedLanguage: A credit reporting company generally can report most negative information for seven years. Information about a lawsuit or a judgment against you can be reported for seven years or until the statute of limitations runs out, whichever is longer. ... However, no one has the right to remove negative information, such as late payments, from a credit report if it is accurate.
claims.notes: CFPB page 'last reviewed: SEP 02, 2026'. The page says 'most negative information' and does not mention foreclosure by name either. Consumer guidance, not the statute.

claims.claim: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau states that housing counselors can provide advice on buying a home, renting, defaults, forbearances, foreclosures and credit issues, and that the counseling agencies on its searchable list are approved by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development and can offer independent advice, often at little or no cost.
claims.quotedLanguage: Housing counselors throughout the country can provide advice on buying a home, renting, defaults, forbearances, foreclosures, and credit issues. ... The counseling agencies on the searchable list are approved by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and they can offer independent advice, often at little or no cost to you.
claims.notes: 'Often at little or no cost' is the CFPB's wording; do not upgrade it to 'free'. A housing counselor is not an attorney; pair with the attorney pointer.

claims.claim: The notice that Idaho Code 45-1602 requires is headed 'NOTICE REQUIRED BY IDAHO LAW'. It opens by explaining what mortgage foreclosure is, tells the owner not to delay seeking advice, names the Idaho Attorney General's website as a source of information, and ends by stating that under Idaho law the owner has five days to rescind or undo certain contracts that relate to transferring interests in property or money in a foreclosure situation.
claims.quotedLanguage: NOTICE REQUIRED BY IDAHO LAW Mortgage foreclosure is a legal proceeding where a lender terminates a borrower's interest in property to satisfy unpaid debt secured by the property. ... Do not delay seeking advice, because the longer you wait, the fewer options you may have. ... Another good source of information is found at the Office of the Idaho Attorney General's website. Under Idaho law, you have five (5) days to rescind or undo certain contracts or agreements that relate to transferring interests in property or money in a foreclosure situation. An attorney or financial professional can tell you more about this option.
claims.notes: Complements vb-cfpa-written-notice-required, which quotes the middle of the same notice. TRAP: the notice text says 'five (5) days'; the operative right in 45-1603 is five BUSINESS days. State both and say which section controls the wording of the right. Do not say the Attorney General endorses any buyer: the notice only names the AG website as an information source.

claims.claim: If a contract covered by Idaho Code 45-1602 was solicited, negotiated or represented to the consumer in Spanish during the foreclosure period, the written notice must be in Spanish, on a form prepared and made available by the office of the attorney general.
claims.quotedLanguage: was solicited, negotiated, or represented to the consumer in the Spanish language, the written notice to be provided to the consumer and set forth in this section shall be in the Spanish language on a form to be prepared and made available by the office of the attorney general
claims.notes: The Spanish form itself was not located on ag.idaho.gov on 2026-11-13. Do not link to it or describe its contents.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1603(3), a notice of cancellation given by mail is effective when deposited in the mail properly addressed with postage prepaid, and notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address specified in the contract is conclusive proof of notice of service.
claims.quotedLanguage: Notice of cancellation, if given by mail, is effective when deposited in the mail properly addressed with postage prepaid. Notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, addressed to the address specified in the contract or agreement, shall be conclusive proof of notice of service.
claims.notes: Subsection (3) only. The right itself and the five-business-day period are in vb-cfpa-five-business-day-rescission. Describe, do not tell a reader how to cancel their own contract.

claims.claim: 12 CFR part 1015 is known as Regulation O. It is issued by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection and applies to persons over which the Federal Trade Commission has jurisdiction under the Federal Trade Commission Act.
claims.quotedLanguage: This part, known as Regulation O, is issued by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection ... This part applies to persons over which the Federal Trade Commission has jurisdiction under the Federal Trade Commission Act.
claims.notes: Current eCFR text retrieved through the renderer API. Future-dated amendments were not separately checked in the Federal Register; futureDatedAmendment=false means none appears in the current eCFR text. Federal regulation, not Idaho law.

claims.claim: Regulation O defines a mortgage assistance relief service as any service, plan or program offered to a consumer in exchange for consideration that is represented to help with, among other things, stopping, preventing or postponing a foreclosure sale, obtaining a loan modification or forbearance, or negotiating a short sale, a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure, or any other disposition of a dwelling other than a sale to a third party who is not the dwelling loan holder. A dwelling is a residential structure of four or fewer units.
claims.quotedLanguage: Mortgage Assistance Relief Service means any service, plan, or program, offered or provided to the consumer in exchange for consideration, that is represented, expressly or by implication, to assist or attempt to assist the consumer with any of the following: ... Stopping, preventing, or postponing any mortgage or deed of trust foreclosure sale for the consumer's dwelling, any repossession of the consumer's dwelling, or otherwise saving the consumer's dwelling from foreclosure or repossession; ... Negotiating, obtaining, or arranging a modification of any term of a dwelling loan, including a reduction in the amount of interest, principal balance, monthly payments, or fees; ... A short sale of a dwelling, ... A deed-in-lieu of foreclosure, or ... Any other disposition of a dwelling other than a sale to a third party who is not the dwelling loan holder. ... Dwelling means a residential structure containing four or fewer units
claims.notes: Current eCFR text retrieved through the renderer API. Future-dated amendments were not separately checked in the Federal Register; futureDatedAmendment=false means none appears in the current eCFR text. Federal regulation, not Idaho law. TRAP: the 'other than a sale to a third party' wording sits in item (6)(iii) only. Item (1) covers any paid service represented to stop or postpone a foreclosure. Never say a buyer is or is not a provider under this rule; quote the definition and stop.

claims.claim: Regulation O defines a mortgage assistance relief service provider as any person that provides, offers to provide or arranges for others to provide such a service, and says the term does not include the dwelling loan holder, the servicer, or their agents or contractors.
claims.quotedLanguage: Mortgage Assistance Relief Service Provider or Provider means any person that provides, offers to provide, or arranges for others to provide, any mortgage assistance relief service. This term does not include: ... The dwelling loan holder, or any agent or contractor of such individual or entity. ... The servicer of a dwelling loan, or any agent or contractor of such individual or entity.
claims.notes: Current eCFR text retrieved through the renderer API. Future-dated amendments were not separately checked in the Federal Register; futureDatedAmendment=false means none appears in the current eCFR text. Federal regulation, not Idaho law.

claims.claim: Under 12 CFR 1015.5(a), it is a violation for a mortgage assistance relief service provider to request or receive payment of any fee or other consideration until the consumer has executed a written agreement with the consumer's loan holder or servicer that incorporates the offer of mortgage relief the provider obtained.
claims.quotedLanguage: It is a violation of this rule for any mortgage assistance relief service provider to: ... Request or receive payment of any fee or other consideration until the consumer has executed a written agreement between the consumer and the consumer's dwelling loan holder or servicer incorporating the offer of mortgage assistance relief the provider obtained from the consumer's dwelling loan holder or servicer;
claims.notes: Current eCFR text retrieved through the renderer API. Future-dated amendments were not separately checked in the Federal Register; futureDatedAmendment=false means none appears in the current eCFR text. Federal regulation, not Idaho law. The trigger is the consumer's signed agreement WITH THE LENDER OR SERVICER, not a signed contract with the relief company. Attorney carve-out is in 1015.7 (fs-rego-attorney-exemption).

claims.claim: When a provider hands the consumer the lender's written offer, 12 CFR 1015.5(b) requires a disclosure on a separate written page stating that the consumer may accept or reject the offer and does not have to pay the provider if the offer is rejected. Section 1015.5(c) also requires a notice from the lender or servicer describing all material differences between the current loan and the loan as it would be if the offer is accepted.
claims.quotedLanguage: “This is an offer of mortgage assistance we obtained from your lender [or servicer]. You may accept or reject the offer. If you reject the offer, you do not have to pay us. ... The disclosure required by this paragraph must be made in a clear and prominent manner, on a separate written page, ... a notice from the consumer's dwelling loan holder or servicer that describes all material differences between the terms, conditions, and limitations associated with the consumer's current mortgage loan and the terms, conditions, and limitations associated with the consumer's mortgage loan if he or she accepts the dwelling loan holder's or servicer's offer
claims.notes: Current eCFR text retrieved through the renderer API. Future-dated amendments were not separately checked in the Federal Register; futureDatedAmendment=false means none appears in the current eCFR text. Federal regulation, not Idaho law.

claims.claim: 12 CFR 1015.4 requires every general commercial communication for a mortgage assistance relief service to state that the company is not associated with the government and that its service is not approved by the government or the consumer's lender. Where the provider has represented that the consumer should stop making loan payments, it must disclose that the consumer could lose the home and damage their credit rating.
claims.quotedLanguage: “(Name of company) is not associated with the government, and our service is not approved by the government or your lender.” ... “Even if you accept this offer and use our service, your lender may not agree to change your loan.” ... “If you stop paying your mortgage, you could lose your home and damage your credit rating.”
claims.notes: Current eCFR text retrieved through the renderer API. Future-dated amendments were not separately checked in the Federal Register; futureDatedAmendment=false means none appears in the current eCFR text. Federal regulation, not Idaho law. The 'lender may not agree' sentence is required only where the provider has represented a result in items (2) to (6) of the definition.

claims.claim: 12 CFR 1015.3 makes it a violation for a mortgage assistance relief service provider to represent that a consumer cannot or should not contact or communicate with his or her lender or servicer, or to misrepresent that its service is affiliated with, endorsed or approved by the United States government, any government agency, a nonprofit housing counselor agency or program, or the consumer's lender or servicer.
claims.quotedLanguage: Representing, expressly or by implication, in connection with the advertising, marketing, promotion, offering for sale, sale, or performance of any mortgage assistance relief service, that a consumer cannot or should not contact or communicate with his or her lender or servicer. ... That a mortgage assistance relief service is affiliated with, endorsed or approved by, or otherwise associated with: ... Any Federal, State, or local government agency, unit, or department, ... Any nonprofit housing counselor agency or program,
claims.notes: Current eCFR text retrieved through the renderer API. Future-dated amendments were not separately checked in the Federal Register; futureDatedAmendment=false means none appears in the current eCFR text. Federal regulation, not Idaho law.

claims.claim: Under 12 CFR 1015.7, an attorney is exempt from most of Regulation O if the attorney provides mortgage assistance relief services as part of the practice of law, is licensed in the state where the consumer resides or the dwelling is located, and complies with state laws and regulations covering the same conduct. That attorney is exempt from the advance-fee section as well only if funds received before performing legal services are deposited in a client trust account and the attorney complies with the state rules for such accounts.
claims.quotedLanguage: An attorney is exempt from this part, with the exception of § 1015.5, if the attorney: ... Provides mortgage assistance relief services as part of the practice of law; ... Is licensed to practice law in the state in which the consumer for whom the attorney is providing mortgage assistance relief services resides or in which the consumer's dwelling is located; ... An attorney who is exempt pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section is also exempt from § 1015.5 if the attorney: ... Deposits any funds received from the consumer prior to performing legal services in a client trust account;
claims.notes: Current eCFR text retrieved through the renderer API. Future-dated amendments were not separately checked in the Federal Register; futureDatedAmendment=false means none appears in the current eCFR text. Federal regulation, not Idaho law.

claims.claim: The Federal Trade Commission says it is illegal for a company to charge upfront for promises to help a homeowner get relief on paying a mortgage, and that under the Mortgage Assistance Relief Services (MARS) Rule a company may not charge anything until it has given the homeowner a written offer of a loan modification or other relief from the lender and the homeowner accepts the offer.
claims.quotedLanguage: It’s illegal for a company to charge you upfront for promises to help you get relief on paying your mortgage. ... The Mortgage Assistance Relief Services (MARS) Rule says it's illegal for a company to charge you a penny until it's given you a written offer for a loan modification or other relief from your lender — and you accept the offer.
claims.notes: Federal consumer guidance (page dated September 2022), not Idaho law.

claims.claim: The FTC describes a 'phony counseling' pattern in which scammers pose as housing counselors, lawyers or government representatives, typically tell the homeowner not to contact the lender, a lawyer or a housing counselor, and may tell the homeowner to make mortgage payments directly to them or to transfer the property deed to them.
claims.quotedLanguage: Scammers say they are: housing counselors or lawyers — or that they represent a law firm or they’re from the government. ... They’ll typically tell you not to contact your lender, lawyer, housing counselor, or credit counselor. They may tell you to make your mortgage payments directly to them — rather than to your lender — or to transfer your property deed to them.
claims.notes: Federal consumer guidance (page dated September 2022), not Idaho law.

claims.claim: The FTC says scammers posing as mortgage loan 'auditors' cannot promise that a forensic loan audit will help a homeowner get a loan modification or any other mortgage relief.
claims.quotedLanguage: Scammers can’t promise that a forensic loan audit will help you get a loan modification or any other mortgage relief.
claims.notes: Federal consumer guidance (page dated September 2022), not Idaho law.

claims.claim: The FTC describes 'rent-to-buy' schemes, in which the homeowner gives up the deed and is told they can stay as a renter and buy the home back later, and 'rescue loan' schemes, in which a document that gives the scammer the deed is buried in a stack of loan papers the homeowner is pressured to sign quickly.
claims.quotedLanguage: These scammers say you can stay there as a renter and your rent payments — supposedly — will go to helping you buy the home back from them later. ... As soon as you give up the deed to your home, the scammers control what happens to it. ... They may pressure you to sign the papers quickly, without giving you a chance to read them thoroughly or giving you time to follow up on any sections that you don’t understand. ... The scammer rushes you because buried in the stack is a document that gives them the deed to your home in exchange for the loan.
claims.notes: Federal consumer guidance (page dated September 2022), not Idaho law. Pair with vb-ftc-deed-transfer-warning and vb-ftc-equity-skimming.

claims.claim: The FTC tells homeowners who are having trouble paying or have received a foreclosure notice to contact their servicer or lender immediately, even if the foreclosure process has already started, and to talk to a certified housing counselor for free help using HUD's list of approved housing counseling agencies. It adds that a homeowner always has the right to contact the lender directly.
claims.quotedLanguage: If you're having trouble paying your mortgage or you've gotten a foreclosure notice, contact your servicer or lender immediately, even if the foreclosure process has already started. ... Talk to a certified housing counselor for free legitimate help. ... You always have the right to contact your lender directly to see whether you have other options.
claims.notes: Federal consumer guidance (page dated September 2022), not Idaho law.

claims.claim: The FTC says a suspected mortgage relief scam should be reported to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and to the state attorney general.
claims.quotedLanguage: If you think you’ve run into a mortgage relief scam, report it to ... the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov ... your state attorney general
claims.notes: Federal consumer guidance (page dated September 2022), not Idaho law.

claims.claim: The FTC says a reputable lawyer does not guarantee results, and that the fact a lawyer works for a company does not mean the company can charge an upfront fee or that it is legitimate. It advises checking that anyone claiming to be a lawyer is licensed in the homeowner's state.
claims.quotedLanguage: A reputable lawyer doesn’t guarantee results, no matter what your circumstances. ... Just because a lawyer works for the company doesn’t mean the company can charge you an upfront fee or that it’s legitimate.
claims.notes: Federal consumer guidance (page dated September 2022), not Idaho law.

claims.claim: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau describes mortgage loan modification scams as schemes to take a homeowner's money, often by a false promise of saving them from foreclosure. Its list of things scammers may do includes asking for fees upfront, promising to get a loan modification, asking the owner to sign over title, asking the owner to sign papers they do not understand, saying payments should go to someone other than the servicer or lender, and telling the owner to stop making mortgage payments.
claims.quotedLanguage: Mortgage loan modification scams are schemes to take your money – often by making a false promise of saving you from foreclosure. ... Ask you to pay fees upfront to receive services ... Ask you to sign over the title to your property ... Ask you to sign papers that you do not understand ... Say you should start making payments to someone other than your servicer or lender ... Tell you to stop making mortgage loan payments altogether
claims.notes: CFPB consumer guidance, page marked 'last reviewed: SEP 11, 2024'. Not Idaho law. The list items are separate bullets on the page, joined here with ellipses.

claims.claim: The CFPB says a homeowner who has been asked for any of the things on its scam list can report the company by submitting a complaint with the CFPB online or by calling (855) 411-CFPB (2372). It also says HUD-approved housing counseling agencies can discuss options with a homeowner who is having trouble paying, and that the state attorney general's office can provide information about state protections and take a complaint.
claims.quotedLanguage: you can report that company by submitting a complaint with the CFPB online or by calling (855) 411-CFPB (2372). ... U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)-approved housing counseling agencies can discuss options with you if you’re having trouble paying your mortgage loan or reverse mortgage loan. ... office for more information about state protections as well as file a complaint.
claims.notes: CFPB consumer guidance, last reviewed SEP 11, 2024. The phone number is the only number in this claim; re-check before each publication refresh.

claims.claim: The CFPB says mortgage relief companies are not allowed to collect any fees until they have provided a written offer from the lender or servicer that the homeowner decides is acceptable, a written document from the lender or servicer describing the key changes to the mortgage, and a reminder that the homeowner may reject the offer without any charge.
claims.quotedLanguage: Mortgage relief companies are not allowed to collect any fees until they have provided you with the following: ... A written offer from your lender or servicer that you decide is acceptable ... A written document from the lender or servicer describing the key changes to your mortgage that would result if you accept the offer ... A reminder that you have the right to reject the offer without any charge
claims.notes: CFPB's plain-language summary of 12 CFR 1015.5. For the legal test use fs-rego-advance-fee-ban.

claims.claim: The CFPB's housing counselor search lists counseling agencies approved by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. The CFPB says they can offer independent advice, often at little or no cost, on topics that include defaults, forbearances and foreclosures, and that not every counselor offers all services.
claims.quotedLanguage: Housing counselors throughout the country can provide advice on buying a home, renting, defaults, forbearances, foreclosures, and credit issues. ... The counseling agencies on the searchable list are approved by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and they can offer independent advice, often at little or no cost to you. ... Not every housing counselor offers all services, so be sure to check the list of services offered by each agency.
claims.notes: CFPB says 'often at little or no cost'; the FTC page says 'free'; the Idaho statutory notice says counselors 'can provide free information'. Use each agency's own word with attribution. Do not promise that counseling is free.

claims.claim: HUD says a housing counseling agency can be found by calling 800-569-4287 or searching online, and describes its housing counseling program as working through HUD participating housing counseling agencies and HUD certified housing counselors.
claims.quotedLanguage: HUD's housing counseling program helps families obtain, sustain and retain their homes. HUD accomplishes this mission through a strong network of HUD participating housing counseling agencies and HUD certified housing counselors. To find a housing counseling agency near you please call 800-569-4287
claims.notes: The HUD page is mostly script-rendered; only this paragraph is in the cached HTML. HUD's own definition of 'approved' or 'certified' was not captured; do not define those terms beyond the quote.

claims.claim: The Idaho Attorney General's Consumer Protection Manual says that 'foreclosure rescue' companies advertise that they can help financially distressed consumers save their homes from foreclosure but often strip consumers of their equity and make them tenants in their own homes. It says consumers should consult a private attorney before signing any contract involving the ownership of their homes.
claims.quotedLanguage: These companies advertise that they can help financially distressed consumers save their homes from foreclosure, but, in fact, they often strip consumers of their equity and make them tenants in their own homes. ... Consumers should consult with a private attorney before they sign any contract involving the ownership of their homes.
claims.notes: State agency publication, guidance not statute. The PDF footer reads 'Rev. 03/21'. The manual's summary says the notice must include 'a five-day right to rescind'; the statute (45-1603) says five business days. Do not quote the manual for the length of the period. The manual says the act applies to 'certain businesses'; use the statute's own words for scope.

claims.claim: The Idaho Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces Idaho's Consumer Protection Act among other consumer laws, accepts consumer complaints through an online Consumer Complaint Form, and lists its phone numbers as 208-334-2424 and toll-free 1-800-432-3545.
claims.quotedLanguage: The Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces various consumer laws, including Idaho’s Consumer Protection Act, Competition Act, Telephone Solicitation Act, and Charitable Solicitation Act. ... If you have a complaint to file with our office, please visit the link below to open the Consumer Complaint Form. ... Phone 208-334-2424 Toll-free 1-800-432-3545
claims.notes: The page gives a 'temporary location' street address (Chinden Campus); do NOT print the address, it is flagged temporary. Phone numbers are FAST-CHANGING: re-check. The page does not mention foreclosure; the link to foreclosure is 45-1605, which routes penalties through title 48 chapter 6 (vb-cfpa-penalties-title-48).

claims.claim: The Idaho Attorney General's office says it assists consumers with complaints against unfair, deceptive and fraudulent business practices, and that a consumer may inform the office without requesting action or may request an informal dispute resolution process.
claims.quotedLanguage: The Office of the Attorney General assists consumers with complaints against unfair, deceptive and fraudulent business practices. ... The consumer also has the option to inform our office without requesting action, or may request an informal dispute resolution process from our investigator team.
claims.notes: General scam-reporting page; it does not mention foreclosure specifically.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 26-31-201 defines 'loan modification activities' as, for compensation or gain or in the expectation of it, engaging in or offering to engage in effecting loan modifications in Idaho, and includes engaging in loan modification activities on behalf of a borrower within 'mortgage brokering activities'. A loan modification is an adjustment or compromise of an existing residential mortgage loan and does not include a refinancing.
claims.quotedLanguage: "Loan modification" means an adjustment or compromise of an existing residential mortgage loan. The term "loan modification" does not include a refinancing transaction. (3) "Loan modification activities" means, for compensation or gain or in the expectation of compensation or gain, engaging in or offering to engage in effecting loan modifications in this state. ... or engaging in loan modification activities on behalf of a borrower.
claims.notes: Definitions only. The license requirement is in 26-31-203 and the exemptions in 26-31-202. Never say whether a named company needs a license.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 26-31-203 says no person, except one exempt under 26-31-202, shall engage in mortgage brokering activities or mortgage lending activities without first obtaining a license from the department, and that a non-exempt person who does so is guilty of a felony on conviction.
claims.quotedLanguage: Any person, except a person exempt under section 26-31-202, Idaho Code, who engages in mortgage brokering activities or mortgage lending activities without first obtaining a license from the department in accordance with this part, shall upon conviction be guilty of a felony.
claims.notes: 'The department' is defined elsewhere in chapter 31 (section not cached); the Department of Finance's own page confirms it is the licensing agency (fs-idfin-licenses-loan-modification-companies). The penalty falls on the unlicensed person, not on the homeowner.

claims.claim: Among the exemptions in Idaho Code 26-31-202 are attorneys authorized to practice in Idaho, to the extent they are retained by their clients to engage in activities authorized by that part and the activities are ancillary to the attorney's representation of the client.
claims.quotedLanguage: Attorneys duly authorized to practice in this state, to the extent that they are retained by their clients to engage in activities authorized by this part and such activities are ancillary to the attorney's representation of the client;
claims.notes: One of eleven exemptions; others include banks, credit unions, government agencies and certain accountants. Do not present this as the full list.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 26-31-211(11) bars a mortgage broker or lender licensee, or a person required to hold that license, from receiving a fee for loan modification activities except under a written agreement that specifies the fee, specifies the terms of the loan for which modification will be sought, and discloses the expected impact of the modification on the monthly payment and length of the loan.
claims.quotedLanguage: Receive a fee for engaging in loan modification activities except pursuant to a written agreement between the person subject to this part and a person seeking a loan modification. The written agreement must specify the amount of the fee that will be charged to the person seeking a loan modification, specify the terms of the loan for which modification will be sought and disclose the expected impact of the loan modification on the monthly payment and length of the loan.
claims.notes: This is the Idaho written-agreement rule. The TIMING of any fee is governed separately by the federal advance-fee ban (fs-rego-advance-fee-ban). Do not merge the two.

claims.claim: The Idaho Department of Finance says the Idaho Residential Mortgage Practices Act charges it with licensing and regulating the mortgage-related activities of mortgage lenders and brokers, mortgage loan modification companies and mortgage loan originators, and that all mortgage licensing is handled through the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System and Registry (NMLS).
claims.quotedLanguage: The Idaho Residential Mortgage Practices Act (IRMPA) charges the Idaho Department of Finance with the responsibility for licensing and regulating the mortgage related activities of mortgage lenders and mortgage brokers, mortgage loan modification companies, independent contractor mortgage loan processors and mortgage underwriters and mortgage loan originators. ... All mortgage licensing is handled through the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System and Registry (NMLS).
claims.notes: Agency page, footer 'last updated: January 20, 2026'. The page also says exempt entities include certain financial institutions, government agencies and, under specific conditions, licensed attorneys and accountants.

claims.claim: The Idaho Department of Finance invites written complaints, with supporting documentation, involving institutions it regulates and alleged violations of its laws and rules, and says a complaint about an institution it does not regulate will be referred to the correct agency. It tells consumers to confirm that a financial services provider is licensed by using the Department's licensee lookup page. It also says it cannot act as a lawyer or give legal advice.
claims.quotedLanguage: the Department invites written complaints and supporting documentation involving institutions regulated by this office and alleged violations of its laws and rules. ... if the Department receives a complaint that involves an institution not regulated by this office, it will be referred to the correct agency. ... Visit the licensee lookup page to confirm the company or individual is licensed with the Department. ... We cannot give you legal advice.
claims.notes: The Department's phone number on the page (208-332-8000) was not put in a claim; do not print it. The page says resolution 'may take several weeks and possibly months' and that there is no guarantee of resolution.

claims.claim: Under 12 CFR 1026.36(c)(3), for a consumer credit transaction secured by a consumer's dwelling, the creditor, assignee or servicer must provide an accurate statement of the total outstanding balance required to pay the obligation in full as of a specified date, sent within a reasonable time and in no case more than seven business days after a written request from the consumer or a person acting on the consumer's behalf; where the statement cannot be provided within seven business days because the loan is in bankruptcy or foreclosure (among other listed reasons), it must be provided within a reasonable time.
claims.quotedLanguage: In connection with a consumer credit transaction secured by a consumer's dwelling, a creditor, assignee or servicer, as applicable, must provide an accurate statement of the total outstanding balance that would be required to pay the consumer's obligation in full as of a specified date. The statement shall be sent within a reasonable time, but in no case more than seven business days, after receiving a written request from the consumer or any person acting on behalf of the consumer. When a creditor, assignee, or servicer, as applicable, is not able to provide the statement within seven business days of such a request because a loan is in bankruptcy or foreclosure, because the loan is a reverse mortgage or shared appreciation mortgage, or because of natural disasters or other similar circumstances, the payoff statement must be provided within a reasonable time.
claims.notes: TRAP: never state the seven-business-day limit without the foreclosure exception in the same breath. A loan in foreclosure is exactly the case where the regulation relaxes the deadline to 'a reasonable time'. The request must be WRITTEN. A creditor or assignee that no longer owns the loan or servicing rights is not subject to the paragraph. Applies to consumer credit secured by a dwelling; do not tell a reader whether their loan qualifies.

claims.claim: The CFPB describes a payoff amount as how much a borrower will have to pay to satisfy the terms of the mortgage loan and completely pay off the debt, says it is different from the current balance, and says it includes interest due through the intended payoff day and may include fees charged and not yet paid.
claims.quotedLanguage: Your payoff amount is how much you will have to pay to satisfy the terms of your mortgage loan and completely pay off your debt. Your payoff amount is different from your current balance. ... Your payoff amount includes the payment of any interest due through the day you intend to pay off your loan. It may also include other fees you have been charged and have not yet paid.
claims.notes: Consumer guidance, not regulation. The page also mentions a possible pre-payment penalty; not used.

claims.claim: Idaho Code 45-1514 provides that upon performance of the obligation secured by a deed of trust, the trustee, upon written request of the beneficiary, shall reconvey the property described in the deed of trust to the grantor; a beneficiary who refuses to make the request or a trustee who refuses to reconvey is liable as provided by law for refusing to execute a discharge or satisfaction of a mortgage.
claims.quotedLanguage: Upon performance of the obligation secured by the deed of trust, the trustee upon written request of the beneficiary shall reconvey the estate of real property described in the deed of trust to the grantor; providing that in the event of such performance and the refusal of any beneficiary to so request or the trustee to so reconvey, as above provided, such beneficiary or trustee shall be liable as provided by law in the case of refusal to execute a discharge or satisfaction of a mortgage on real property.
claims.notes: The section sets NO deadline for the reconveyance and does not itself state the liability; it points to the mortgage-discharge rule (Idaho Code 45-915, read but not claimed here). Do not state a dollar penalty or a number of days from this section.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1202, a title insurer or title agent may reconvey a deed of trust under the procedure in 45-1203 if it has fully paid the obligation secured by the trust deed or possesses satisfactory evidence of payment in full, whether or not it is named as trustee.
claims.quotedLanguage: A title insurer or title agent may reconvey a trust deed pursuant to the procedure prescribed in section 45-1203, Idaho Code, if the obligation secured by the trust deed shall have been fully paid by the title insurer or title agent that is permitted to reconvey the trust deed pursuant to section 45-1203, Idaho Code, or such title insurer or title agent shall possess satisfactory evidence of such payment in full. A title insurer or title agent may provide a reconveyance under section 45-1203, Idaho Code, whether or not it is then named as trustee under a trust deed.
claims.notes: Permissive ('may'). This is a backstop for when the beneficiary does not reconvey; it is not the ordinary route and it is the title company's option, not the seller's right.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1203, a title insurer or title agent may, not less than 30 days after payment in full of the obligation secured by the trust deed and receipt of satisfactory evidence of that payment, give the beneficiary or servicer a notice of intent to reconvey; 60 days must then elapse, and if no objection under 45-1204 has been received by the end of that period the title insurer or title agent may execute, acknowledge and record a reconveyance of the trust deed.
claims.quotedLanguage: A title insurer or title agent may execute and record a reconveyance of a trust deed upon compliance with the following procedure: (1) Not less than thirty (30) days after payment in full of the obligation secured by the trust deed and receipt of satisfactory evidence of payment in full has been effected, the title insurer or title agent may either: (a) mail a notice by certified mail with postage prepaid, return receipt requested, to the beneficiary or a servicer ... (2) Sixty (60) days shall elapse following the mailing, in the case of certified mail, or delivery, in the case of hand delivery, of the notice prescribed in subsection (1) of this section. (3) If the title insurer or title agent has not upon expiration of that sixty (60) day period received any objection under section 45-1204, Idaho Code, the title insurer or title agent may then execute, acknowledge, and record a reconveyance of the trust deed
claims.notes: TRAP: these are the day counts of the title-company backstop only. Never write that 'reconveyance takes 90 days' or that a seller must wait for it; a beneficiary can request reconveyance under 45-1514 at any time. 45-1203(4) adds that a reconveyance under this chapter does not itself discharge any personal obligation that was secured.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1506(12), the grantor, a successor in interest in the trust property, a beneficiary under a subordinate deed of trust or a person with a subordinate lien of record may, at any time within 115 days of the recording of the notice of default where the power of sale is to be exercised, pay the beneficiary the entire amount then due (including costs and expenses actually incurred in enforcing the obligation, a reasonable trustee's fee and attorney's fees as provided in the promissory note) other than the portion of principal that would not then be due had no default occurred; doing so cures the default, the proceedings are dismissed or discontinued, and the obligation and deed of trust are reinstated as if no acceleration had occurred.
claims.quotedLanguage: the grantor or his successor in interest in the trust property or any part thereof, or any beneficiary under a subordinate deed of trust or any person having a subordinate lien or encumbrance of record thereon, at any time within one hundred fifteen (115) days of the recording of the notice of default under such deed of trust, if the power of sale therein is to be exercised, or otherwise at any time prior to the entry of a decree of foreclosure, may pay to the beneficiary or their successors in interest, respectively, the entire amount then due under the terms of the deed of trust and the obligation secured thereby, including costs and expenses actually incurred in enforcing the terms of such obligation and a reasonable trustee's fee ... and attorney's fees as may be provided in the promissory note, other than such portion of the principal as would not then be due had no default occurred, and thereby cure the default theretofore existing, and thereupon, all proceedings theretofore had or instituted shall be dismissed or discontinued and the obligation and deed of trust shall be reinstated and shall be and remain in force and effect, the same as if no acceleration had occurred.
claims.notes: TRAP: the 115 days run from the RECORDING OF THE NOTICE OF DEFAULT, not from the notice of sale and not counted back from the sale date. Never write 'you can cure up to the sale'. The trustee's fee is capped by 45-1502(6) (elided from the quote, not researched here). Source idcode-45-1506 is already in the registry; add this claim id to its claimsSupported at merge.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1506(8), a trustee's sale is held on the date in the notice of sale unless postponed under that subsection or under 45-1506B (stay or injunctive relief); the trustee may postpone the sale upon request of the beneficiary by public announcement at the time and place originally fixed, to a date not more than 30 days after the date from which it is postponed, and a postponed sale may itself be postponed in the same manner.
claims.quotedLanguage: The sale shall be held on the date and at the time and place designated in the notice of sale or notice of rescheduled sale as provided in section 45-1506A, Idaho Code, unless the sale is postponed as provided in this subsection or as provided in section 45-1506B, Idaho Code, respecting the effect of an intervening stay or injunctive relief order. ... The trustee may postpone the sale of the property upon request of the beneficiary by publicly announcing at the time and place originally fixed for the sale the postponement to a stated subsequent date and hour. No sale may be postponed to a date more than thirty (30) days subsequent to the date from which the sale is postponed. A postponed sale may itself be postponed in the same manner and within the same time limitations as provided in this subsection.
claims.notes: Used to support one point only: the subsection gives the postponement request to the BENEFICIARY and names no right for an owner or buyer. 45-1506A (rescheduled sale) and 45-1506B (stays) were not researched for this page; do not describe them. Source idcode-45-1506 is already in the registry.

claims.claim: Under Idaho Code 45-1505, a trustee may foreclose a trust deed by advertisement and sale only if, among other conditions, the trustee or beneficiary has recorded a notice of default in each county where the property sits; the trustee must mail that notice to any individual who owns an interest in the property, accompanied by a statutory notice in 12-point boldface type that includes the warning not to delay seeking advice because the longer the owner waits, the fewer options the owner may have.
claims.quotedLanguage: The trustee may foreclose a trust deed by advertisement and sale under this act if: ... (3) The trustee or beneficiary shall have (a) filed for record in the office of the recorder in each county wherein the trust property, or some part or parcel, is situated, a notice of default ... In addition, the trustee shall mail the notice required in this section to any individual who owns an interest in property which is the subject of this section. Such notice shall be accompanied by and affixed to the following notice in twelve (12) point boldface type ... Do not delay seeking advice, because the longer you wait, the fewer options you may have.
claims.notes: The statutory notice text in 45-1505 also says 'five (5) days' to rescind; the operative right in 45-1603 is five BUSINESS days (see vb-cfpa-five-business-day-rescission). Conditions (1), (2) and (4) of 45-1505 are not summarised by this claim.

claims.claim: 12 CFR 1024.41 states that nothing in the section imposes a duty on a servicer to provide any borrower with any specific loss mitigation option, and it applies a narrower set of requirements to small servicers.
claims.quotedLanguage: Nothing in § 1024.41 imposes a duty on a servicer to provide any borrower with any specific loss mitigation option. ... A small servicer shall be subject to the prohibition on foreclosure referral in paragraph (f)(1) of this section.
claims.notes: Must accompany every mention of the 1024.41 review: the rule is procedural and promises no outcome. Scope of Subpart C (12 CFR 1024.30: which loans and servicers are covered, the principal-residence condition) was NOT researched; never tell a reader the rule applies to their loan.

claims.claim: Under 12 CFR 1024.41(c)(1), if a servicer receives a complete loss mitigation application more than 37 days before a foreclosure sale, then within 30 days of receiving it the servicer must evaluate the borrower for all loss mitigation options available to the borrower and give written notice of which options, if any, it will offer; a complete application is one in which the servicer has received all the information it requires from the borrower.
claims.quotedLanguage: A complete loss mitigation application means an application in connection with which a servicer has received all the information that the servicer requires from a borrower in evaluating applications for the loss mitigation options available to the borrower. ... if a servicer receives a complete loss mitigation application more than 37 days before a foreclosure sale, then, within 30 days of receiving the complete loss mitigation application, a servicer shall: (i) Evaluate the borrower for all loss mitigation options available to the borrower; and (ii) Provide the borrower with a notice in writing stating the servicer's determination of which loss mitigation options, if any, it will offer to the borrower on behalf of the owner or assignee of the mortgage.
claims.notes: TRAP: 'COMPLETE' application and 'MORE THAN 37 days before a foreclosure sale' are both conditions; never drop either. The paragraph opens 'Except as provided in paragraph (c)(4)(ii)'. State with sk-loss-mit-no-duty-specific-option.

claims.claim: Under 12 CFR 1024.41(g), if a borrower submits a complete loss mitigation application after the servicer has made the first foreclosure notice or filing but more than 37 days before a foreclosure sale, the servicer may not move for foreclosure judgment or order of sale or conduct a foreclosure sale unless the servicer has sent notice that the borrower is not eligible for any option and the appeal process is inapplicable, unused in time or denied, the borrower rejects all options offered, or the borrower fails to perform under a loss mitigation agreement.
claims.quotedLanguage: If a borrower submits a complete loss mitigation application after a servicer has made the first notice or filing required by applicable law for any judicial or non-judicial foreclosure process but more than 37 days before a foreclosure sale, a servicer shall not move for foreclosure judgment or order of sale, or conduct a foreclosure sale, unless: (1) The servicer has sent the borrower a notice pursuant to paragraph (c)(1)(ii) of this section that the borrower is not eligible for any loss mitigation option and the appeal process in paragraph (h) of this section is not applicable, the borrower has not requested an appeal within the applicable time period for requesting an appeal, or the borrower's appeal has been denied; (2) The borrower rejects all loss mitigation options offered by the servicer; or (3) The borrower fails to perform under an agreement on a loss mitigation option.
claims.notes: TRAP: this is a federal limit on the SERVICER's conduct with three exits; it is not a right to stop a sale and must never be written as 'applying stops the foreclosure'. Complete application + more than 37 days are conditions. Paragraph (i) (duplicative requests) can remove the protection for a repeat application; not claimed.

claims.claim: The CFPB defines a short sale as a sale of a home for less than what is owed on the mortgage, classes it as a type of loss mitigation, and says that if the lender or servicer agrees to it the borrower may be able to sell the home to pay off the mortgage even if the sale price or proceeds are less than the remaining balance.
claims.quotedLanguage: A short sale, which is a type of loss mitigation, is a sale of your home for less than what you owe on your mortgage. ... If your lender or servicer agrees to a short sale, you may be able to sell your home to pay off your mortgage, even if the sale price or proceeds turn out to be less than the balance remaining on your mortgage.
claims.notes: Federal consumer guidance, not Idaho law. 'If your lender or servicer agrees' is the operative condition; always carry it.

claims.claim: The CFPB says that a borrower in a state where the borrower is responsible for a deficiency (the difference between the value of the property and the amount still owed) will want to ask the lender to waive the deficiency before going through with a short sale, and to get any waiver in writing.
claims.quotedLanguage: If you live in a state in which you are responsible for any deficiency, which is the difference between the value of your property and the amount you still owe on your mortgage loan, you will want to ask your lender to waive the deficiency before you go through with a short sale. ... If the lender waives the deficiency, get the waiver in writing and keep it for your records.
claims.notes: TRAP: the CFPB sentence is conditional on state law. This page does NOT say whether or how Idaho allows a deficiency after a short sale (Idaho Code 45-1512 belongs to the short-sale page and was not researched here). Always pair with a pointer to an Idaho attorney.

claims.claim: The CFPB says a housing counselor through a HUD-approved agency is trained and certified by the government to help a homeowner assess their financial situation and evaluate options when having trouble paying the mortgage, that HUD-approved housing counseling agencies provide foreclosure prevention counseling free of charge and can help the homeowner talk to the mortgage servicer, and that a counselor can be reached through the HOPE Hotline at (888) 995-HOPE (4673) or by calling the CFPB at (855) 411-CFPB (2372).
claims.quotedLanguage: A housing counselor though a HUD-approved agency is specially trained and certified by the government to help you assess your financial situation, evaluate options if you are having trouble paying your mortgage loan, and make a plan to get you help with your mortgage. ... HUD-approved housing counseling agencies provide foreclosure prevention counseling free of charge. They can also help you talk to your mortgage servicer and understand any options your servicer has offered. ... Call the HOPE Hotline, open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, at (888) 995-HOPE (4673). Call the CFPB at (855) 411-CFPB (2372) to be connected to a housing counselor over the phone.
claims.notes: 'though a HUD-approved agency' is the CFPB's own typo, kept verbatim in the quote. 'Free of charge' is stated for FORECLOSURE PREVENTION counseling specifically. Phone numbers are FAST-CHANGING relative to the rest; re-check before reprinting.

claims.claim: The CFPB says a housing counselor at a HUD-approved agency cannot promise that a homeowner will get to keep the home, and that a homeowner facing imminent foreclosure or served with legal papers may also need to consult an attorney.
claims.quotedLanguage: A housing counselor at a HUD-approved agency can't promise that you will get to keep your home. They will help you look at your options and make a decision that's right for you. If you are facing imminent foreclosure or have been served with legal papers, you may also need to consult an attorney
claims.notes: Keeps the counselor referral honest: help with options, no promised outcome.
